title: How to Apply for SASSA Grants (Online & In Person) in 2026
description: Step-by-step guide to applying for any SASSA grant in 2026 — SRD R370 online, permanent grants online via the SASSA Services Portal, or in person at a SASSA office. Includes required documents and what happens after you apply.

steps.title: Choose the Right Grant for Your Situation
steps.content:
Before applying, confirm which SASSA grant fits your circumstances. The main options are:
  • SRD R370 grant — for unemployed South Africans aged 18–59 with income below R624/month. Applied for online only.
  • Older Persons (Old Age) Grant — for citizens aged 60+ who pass the means test. Pays R2,400/month (under 75) or R2,420 (75+).
  • Disability Grant — for adults aged 18–59 with a medical disability preventing employment. Pays R2,400/month.
  • Child Support Grant — for primary caregivers of children under 18. Pays R580/month per child.
  • Foster Child Grant — for foster parents with a children's court order. Pays R1,300/month.
  • Care Dependency Grant — for caregivers of children with severe disabilities. Pays R2,400/month.
  • Grant-in-Aid — a R580/month top-up for Old Age or Disability recipients who need full-time care.
  • War Veterans Grant — for WWII or Korean War veterans. Pays R2,420/month.
You can only receive one primary grant at a time (plus the Grant-in-Aid top-up). Use our eligibility checker and browse the grant guides to compare options.
tips: The SRD grant is the only grant you can apply for entirely online via srd.sassa.gov.za.
Permanent grants can now be started online via the SASSA Services Portal, but you may still be asked to visit an office for documents.

steps.title: Gather Your Required Documents
steps.content:
Every SASSA grant application needs the same core documents:
  • Your 13-digit South African ID — green ID book, smart ID card, or temporary ID certificate. Refugees and asylum seekers need their permit.
  • Proof of income — payslips, pension slips, or bank statements for the last 3 months. If you have no income, bring an affidavit.
  • Proof of residence — utility bill or affidavit confirming your address.
  • Proof of marital status — marriage certificate, divorce decree, or spousal death certificate if applicable (for means-tested grants).
  • A valid bank account in your name — for grant payments, or collect via Postbank/retail.
  • Grant-specific documents — medical assessment reports for Disability/Care Dependency, a children's court order for Foster Child, or proof of military service for the War Veterans Grant.
See our complete document checklist for details.
tips: If you lost your ID book, apply for a replacement from the Department of Home Affairs before starting your SASSA application.
Certified copies of documents are generally accepted — get them certified at any police station.

steps.title: Apply Online (Fastest Option)
steps.content:
Two official online portals are used for SASSA applications in 2026:
  • SRD grant: go to srd.sassa.gov.za, enter your 13-digit ID number and mobile number, provide banking details, and submit. The Moya App also routes SRD applications into the same system.
  • Permanent grants: go to services.sassa.gov.za, the official SASSA Services Portal. Register an account, log in, and complete the online application for the Older Persons, Disability, Child Support, Foster Child, Care Dependency, Grant-in-Aid, or War Veterans Grant. You will be guided through the steps and may need to upload supporting documents.
Always check that you are on the official .gov.za domain — never pay anyone to apply on your behalf. SASSA applications are free.
tips: For the SRD application you will receive an SMS confirmation once submitted — keep it as proof.
The SASSA Services Portal requires you to register and verify your identity the first time you log in.

steps.title: Apply In Person at a SASSA Office (If You Prefer)
steps.content:
You can still apply in person at your nearest SASSA office. Bring your ID and all supporting documents listed in step 2. At the office:
  1. Take a queue ticket for the application counter.
  2. Tell the officer which grant you are applying for.
  3. Complete the application form with their help — check that every detail matches your ID.
  4. Submit your documents and receive a receipt with a reference number.
Go early (offices open at 08:00) to avoid long queues, especially at month-end. Find your nearest office on our offices page.
tips: Bring a pen and write your phone number clearly so SASSA can reach you.
Ask for a case reference number and keep the stamped receipt — it is your proof of application.

steps.title: What Happens After You Apply
steps.content:
After submitting your application:
  • Processing time: SASSA aims to process most grant applications within 30 to 90 days. The SRD grant is assessed on a monthly cycle, with status updates typically available after the 15th of each month.
  • Means test: SASSA will verify your income and assets against the threshold for your grant. For the SRD, bank accounts are checked for monthly deposits over R624.
  • Possible assessments: For the Disability and Care Dependency Grants, a state medical assessment is required. A SASSA official may also visit your home for Grant-in-Aid or Foster Child verification.
  • Check your status: Use our status check tool, the official SRD portal, the WhatsApp line, or call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11.
  • If declined: You can appeal the decision via the Independent Tribunal. See our appeal guide.
tips: Your grant is paid from the date of application, not the approval date — so apply as soon as you qualify.
If your status shows 'Pending' for more than 90 days, contact your local SASSA office with your reference number.

faqs.q: Can I apply for a SASSA grant online in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The SRD grant is applied for online at srd.sassa.gov.za. Most permanent grants can now also be started online via the official SASSA Services Portal at services.sassa.gov.za. You may still be asked to visit a SASSA office to submit physical documents.

faqs.q: How long does a SASSA grant application take?
faqs.a: Submitting the application takes about 15 minutes online. SASSA then processes it within 30 to 90 days. The SRD grant is assessed on a monthly cycle with status updates usually available after the 15th of each month.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to apply for a SASSA grant?
faqs.a: No. All SASSA grant applications are completely free. Anyone who asks you to pay to apply or to 'speed up' your application is a scammer. Report them to the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply for a SASSA grant?
faqs.a: You need your 13-digit South African ID, proof of income (or an affidavit if you have none), proof of residence, and a bank account in your name. Grant-specific documents like medical reports or court orders may also be required.

faqs.q: Can I apply for more than one SASSA grant?
faqs.a: No. You can only receive one primary SASSA grant at a time. The only exception is the Grant-in-Aid, which is a supplementary top-up for people already receiving the Old Age or Disability Grant.

title: How to Appeal a Declined SASSA SRD Application (Step-by-Step)
description: Your SASSA SRD R370 application was declined — that is not the end of the road. Every declined applicant can dispute the decision, first with a SASSA reconsideration and then with an appeal to the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA). This step-by-step 2026 guide shows you exactly how to find your decline reason, gather the right evidence, submit your appeal online or by WhatsApp, track it, and what to do if the appeal also fails.
imageAlt: Paper document with a stamp reading 'Appeal'

steps.title: Find Out Exactly Why Your SRD Was Declined
steps.content: Every decline has a reason, and a strong appeal is built around that reason. Log in at the official SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za with your ID number and cellphone number, or use our SRD status checker, and read the exact status next to your application. The most common 2026 decline reasons are: UIF registered, NSFAS registered, income source detected, identity verification failed, bank details pending, means test failed, and age outside range. Before you do anything else, read the page for your specific decline reason on our site so you understand what SASSA's automated system actually flagged.
tips: Write down your exact decline reason and the date it appeared on the portal — you will need both when you appeal.
Do not wait. The reconsideration window is 30 days and starts from the day the decision appears.

steps.title: Understand the Two-Step Appeals Process
steps.content: There are two separate levels of dispute, and you must do them in order. Step one is a reconsideration: you ask SASSA to look at your application again within 30 days of the decline, free of charge, at srd.sassa.gov.za. Step two is an appeal to the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA): you have 90 days from the date of the reconsideration outcome to take the case further at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za. If you try to appeal straight to the Tribunal without a reconsideration first, your case will usually be sent back and you will lose time.
tips: You do not need a lawyer for either step — both are designed for applicants to complete on their own.
Keep every reference number you receive: the SRD application number, the reconsideration number, and the ITSAA case number.

steps.title: Gather Evidence That Matches Your Decline Reason
steps.content: Your appeal is only as strong as your proof. If SASSA flagged you as UIF or NSFAS registered, get an official letter or statement from that fund showing you are not registered or are not receiving payments. If you received income source detected, prepare bank statements showing the money was a family transfer, stokvel payout, or a once-off gift and not a salary. If identity verification failed, make sure your ID number, cellphone number and banking details are exactly right before you submit. Where you cannot get a document, a sworn affidavit can carry the explanation.
tips: Photograph or scan your documents clearly and save them as PDF or JPG before you start the online form.
Never hide real income — SASSA cross-checks your bank accounts, UIF and NSFAS records every month.

steps.title: Submit Your Reconsideration Online
steps.content: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za and log in with your ID number and cellphone number. Under your declined application you will see the option to apply for reconsideration. Answer the questions honestly, upload your supporting documents, and confirm the submission. You will receive an SMS with a reference number. Most reconsideration outcomes are sent within 30 days. If SASSA upholds the decline, the same portal will show that you now have the option to appeal to the Independent Tribunal.
tips: Take a screenshot of each step so you have proof if something goes wrong and you need to contact SASSA.
Use a stable internet connection — the SRD portal times out if you leave the page idle.

steps.title: Appeal to the Independent Tribunal (ITSAA)
steps.content: If your reconsideration is refused, go to srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za to lodge a formal appeal with the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals. Register with your ID number and mobile number, select the SRD R370 grant and the exact decline reason, explain in your own words why the decision is wrong, and attach the same evidence you used in the reconsideration. The Tribunal aims to decide within 90 days, and the outcome is sent by SMS. If the portal will not accept your phone number, you can email the Tribunal instead.
tips: Lodge your appeal before the 90-day window closes - the Tribunal counts from the date of the reconsideration outcome.
Keep the SMS or email confirming your appeal submission - you need the case number to track it.
If the portal rejects your phone number, email the Tribunal using the contact details on srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za.

steps.title: Track Your Appeal and Know the Timeline
steps.content: Once you have submitted, you can follow progress on the ITSAA portal using your case number. If a decision goes in your favour, SASSA pays the back pay for the months your grant was wrongly stopped, into the bank account or payment method on your application. If your appeal runs past 90 days without a decision, contact the Tribunal directly. For a full breakdown of what happens at every stage, from day 0 to the decision, see our guide to SASSA appeal timelines.
tips: Check your SMS inbox and your SRD portal status every week while the appeal is open.
The decision SMS sometimes takes a day or two longer than the portal update — trust the portal.

steps.title: What to Do If Your Appeal Is Declined
steps.content: A refused appeal does not ban you from the grant. Because the SRD R370 application window reopens each month, you can apply again in a later application period as long as you still qualify: your income must be below R624 per month and you must be between the ages of 18 and 59. If the decline reason was income-related, sort out the issue that changed your circumstances before re-applying. If you believe the system is still wrong, contact the SASSA SRD call centre and ask for a manual check of your file, with your ID number at hand.
tips: A re-application is a brand-new application, not an extension — answer every question again and keep your proof.
Keep all reference numbers and SMS messages until the new application is approved.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a declined SASSA SRD grant?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the decline to submit a SASSA reconsideration at srd.sassa.gov.za. If that is refused, you then have 90 days from the reconsideration outcome to appeal to the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA).

faqs.q: What is the difference between a reconsideration and an ITSAA appeal?
faqs.a: A reconsideration is the first step, where SASSA re-examines your application itself within 30 days. An ITSAA appeal is the second step, heard by the independent Tribunal at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za, and you can only lodge it after a reconsideration has been refused.

faqs.q: Can I appeal more than once?
faqs.a: For the same decline you get one reconsideration and one appeal. However, you can submit a brand-new SRD application in a later monthly application window if you still meet the income and age rules.

faqs.q: Will I get back pay if my appeal succeeds?
faqs.a: Yes. If a reconsideration or Tribunal appeal is decided in your favour, SASSA pays the grant you missed from the date the payments stopped, into your bank account or your chosen payment method.

The ITSAA appeal window is 90 days from the outcome of your reconsideration. If you missed it, you can still try to lodge a late appeal on srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za and explain the reason for the delay — late appeals are considered in some cases. Because the SRD is reassessed every month, the most reliable path is simply to reapply in the next monthly window if you still qualify (income below R624, aged 18 to 59). For a missed reconsideration (30 days from the decline), contact the SASSA SRD call centre on 0800 60 10 11 and ask for a manual review of your file.
faqs.q: I missed the 90-day appeal deadline — what can I do?

faqs.a: If srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za will not load or rejects your phone number, first check that your ID number and cellphone number exactly match the ones on your SRD application. Try a different browser, clear your cache, or use a laptop instead of a phone. If the portal still will not accept your number, you can email the Independent Tribunal instead — the Tribunal's contact details are listed on the srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za website. As a last resort, contact the SASSA SRD call centre on 0800 60 10 11 or visit a SASSA office with your ID and your decline SMS so an agent can assist.
faqs.q: The appeal portal is not working / it won't accept my phone number — what do I do?

title: How to Apply for the SASSA Child Support Grant in 2026
description: Step-by-step guide to applying for the SASSA Child Support Grant in 2026: eligibility rules and the income means test, the documents you need, how to apply online, in person or by post, what happens after you apply, the payment amount and dates, common mistakes that cause delays, and what to do if your application is declined.
imageAlt: Family hands gathered together representing support for children

steps.title: Check You Meet the 2026 Eligibility Rules
steps.content: Before you apply, check that you qualify. The child must be under 18 and must live with you as the primary caregiver — the person responsible for the child's daily needs. You and the child must be South African citizens, permanent residents, or refugees. Finally, you must pass the means test: if you are single, your monthly income must be R5,800 or less, and if you are married, your combined household income must be R11,600 or less. The grant is paid at R580 per child per month.
tips: The means test looks at your gross monthly income before tax, so count your full pay.
Working parents can still qualify — the child support threshold is much higher than the SRD limit.

steps.title: Gather Your Documents Before You Apply
steps.content: Having the right documents ready saves you a second visit. You need your 13-digit South African ID (green ID book or smart ID card), the child's birth certificate (an unabridged copy is preferred), the child's ID number, proof of residence, and proof of income — payslips, bank statements, or an affidavit if you have no income. If you are not the child's parent, you also need an affidavit from the biological parent explaining the situation. See our full document checklist for the complete list.
tips: An unabridged birth certificate avoids delays when the child's parents are not married.
Make copies of everything and keep the originals — SASSA returns your documents after the application.

steps.title: Choose Where to Apply: Online, In Person, or by Post
steps.content: You have three options. Online is the fastest: register at the official SASSA services portal at services.sassa.gov.za and complete the application in one sitting. In person at your nearest SASSA office is the most popular option because a SASSA officer checks your documents on the spot. If you cannot travel, you can post your completed application form and certified copies to your provincial SASSA office. Whichever you choose, start with the eligibility rules and documents above so your application is complete the first time.
tips: Find your nearest SASSA office and its opening hours on our SASSA offices page before you travel.
If you apply online, you may still be asked to visit an office to verify your ID and documents.

steps.title: Submit Your Application Step by Step
steps.content: At a SASSA office, take a queue ticket, complete the application form with help from the officer, and hand over your documents — it is recommended to bring the child with you. Online, log in to services.sassa.gov.za, select the Child Support Grant, fill in your details and the child's details, and upload your documents. In both cases you will be asked about your income, your living situation, and the child's living arrangements. Answer everything truthfully — SASSA checks the information against national records.
tips: A court order, social worker report, or affidavit helps if you need to prove you are the primary caregiver.
Give SASSA a cellphone number you will keep for at least three months — approval is sent by SMS.

steps.title: Understand What Happens After You Apply
steps.content: You will receive a receipt with a reference number — keep it safe, it is your proof of application. SASSA processes applications within 30 to 90 days and will send an SMS when a decision is made. If approved, payments start and are made each month from around the 6th, at R580 per child. You will need a bank account, a SASSA payment card, or a cash collection point to receive the money. Your grant continues until the child turns 18 or your circumstances change.
tips: Set up your bank details correctly — see our guide to changing your banking details if you need to update them.
If you care for more than one child, you receive the grant amount for each qualifying child.

steps.title: Avoid These Common Application Mistakes
steps.content: Most declined or delayed child support applications come down to the same mistakes: a misspelled ID number or surname that does not match the child's birth certificate, income declared that accidentally exceeds the threshold, a missing affidavit for a non-parent caregiver, incorrect bank details, or no proof of residence. Double-check every number and letter before you submit, and if your details change after applying, tell SASSA immediately. A small error at the application stage can hold up a grant for months.
tips: Re-read the form once, slowly, before handing it over — especially the ID numbers and dates of birth.
If you move house or change jobs, update SASSA right away to protect your grant.

steps.title: What to Do If Your Application Is Declined
steps.content: If SASSA declines your application, you will receive the reason in the SMS. Many declines are for a simple data error or a means test result that can be disputed. You have 30 days to ask SASSA to reconsider the decision, and then 90 days to appeal to the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals if needed — the same process we explain in our guide to appealing a declined SASSA application. If the reason was that your income is over the threshold, wait until your income drops and re-apply with updated proof.
tips: Check your decline reason on our status pages so you fix the real issue before re-applying.
Do not submit a duplicate application while an existing one is still being processed — it can confuse the system.

faqs.q: How much is the SASSA Child Support Grant in 2026?
faqs.a: The Child Support Grant is R580 per child per month in 2026. You receive that amount for each child who qualifies, so a caregiver with two qualifying children receives double.

faqs.q: How long does a Child Support Grant application take?
faqs.a: SASSA says applications are normally processed within 30 to 90 days. You will get an SMS with the outcome, and if approved, the first payment follows shortly after.

faqs.q: Can a grandparent or a working parent apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Any primary caregiver can apply, including grandparents and other relatives — with an affidavit if you are not the parent. Working parents can also qualify as long as their monthly income is below the threshold of R5,800 if single, or R11,600 combined if married.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the Child Support Grant online?
faqs.a: Yes, you can start and complete your application online at services.sassa.gov.za. You may still need to visit a SASSA office once to verify your ID and original documents.

title: How to Reinstate a Lapsed or Suspended Grant
description: If your SASSA grant has been suspended or has lapsed, this guide walks you through the steps to get it reinstated and recover back payments.

steps.title: Why was my grant suspended?
steps.content:
A grant can be suspended for several reasons, including:
  • A change in your financial circumstances.
  • Failure to collect the grant for three consecutive months.
  • You were admitted to a state institution for more than three months.
  • You are no longer eligible for the grant.
tips: SASSA should send you a letter explaining why your grant was suspended.
You can also check your status online or by calling the SASSA helpline.

steps.title: How to apply for restoration
steps.content:
To have your grant reinstated, you must apply for restoration within 90 days of the suspension. You will need to visit your nearest SASSA office and bring the following documents:
  • Your 13-digit bar-coded ID.
  • Proof of your current address.
  • Any documents that prove you are still eligible for the grant (e.g., a recent payslip, a doctor's letter).
tips: There is no fee to apply for restoration.
If you are too sick to visit a SASSA office, you can have someone apply on your behalf.

steps.title: What happens next?
steps.content: SASSA will review your application for restoration. If your application is successful, your grant will be reinstated and you will receive back payments from the date it was suspended. If your application is denied, you have the right to appeal the decision.
tips: The restoration process can take up to three months.
Keep your receipt as proof of your application.

title: Lost or Changed Your SASSA Phone Number? How to Update It in 2026
description: If you lost access to the phone number registered with SASSA, you cannot check your status, receive OTPs, or change banking details. This guide shows you how to update your number.
imageAlt: Person holding a smartphone with a lost SIM card next to it

steps.title: Understand Why a Lost Number Blocks Your Grant
steps.content: Your SASSA SRD account is linked to the cellphone number you used when applying. Every time you log into the SRD portal, SASSA sends a one-time PIN (OTP) via SMS to that number. If you lost the number, you cannot log in. You also cannot change your banking details, submit an appeal, or check your status online. This is the most common reason people get stuck with a 'Bank Details Pending' status and cannot fix it.
tips: SASSA will not send OTPs to a new number automatically — you must request the change.
If you still have your old SIM card but no network, try inserting it into another phone to receive OTPs.

steps.title: Try the SASSA Self-Service Portal First
steps.content: Before visiting a SASSA office, try the new 2026 SASSA Self-Service Portal at www.sassa.gov.za. Click on 'Self-Service Portal' and log in with your 13-digit ID number and the cellphone number registered with SASSA. If you can still receive SMS on your old number (e.g., you have the SIM but lost the phone), you can update your contact details directly in the portal — including your cellphone number, address, and other profile information. This method works 24/7 and takes about 5 minutes.
tips: The self-service portal requires you to receive an OTP on your current registered number — if you cannot, skip to the SASSA office visit below.
You need a smartphone with a camera for facial recognition if the portal prompts for biometric verification.

steps.title: Visit Your Nearest SASSA Office in Person (if the portal does not work)
steps.content: If you cannot receive OTPs to your old number and the self-service portal is not an option, you must visit a SASSA office in person. Bring your original 13-digit South African ID book or smart ID card. If you have a SIM swap confirmation from your mobile network provider, bring that as well. Explain to the SASSA officer that you need your phone number updated on the SRD system.
tips: Go early in the morning to avoid long queues (offices open at 08:00).
Bring a pen — you may need to fill out a change of details form.

steps.title: Complete the Change of Contact Details Form
steps.content: The SASSA officer will give you a form to fill in. You need to write your full name, ID number, old phone number (if you remember it), and the new cellphone number you want to register. The new number must be a valid South African number that is RICA-compliant and registered in your name. Keep a copy of the completed form with the SASSA stamp as proof of your visit.
tips: Write clearly and check your new number three times before submitting.
Ask the officer for a case reference number so you can follow up.

steps.title: Wait for the Update to Be Processed
steps.content: After submitting the form, SASSA takes 3 to 7 working days to update your phone number in the system. Once the update is complete, you will receive a confirmation SMS on your new number. You can then log into the SRD portal using your new number. If after 10 working days you still have not received the SMS, call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11.
tips: Do not ask SASSA to update a number that is not RICA-registered in your name.
If you urgently need to check your status, use the WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) — it uses your WhatsApp number, not your SASSA registered number.

steps.title: Update Your Number on the Moya App (Alternative)
steps.content: If you have access to the Moya App, you can sometimes update your contact information through its SASSA service channel. Open Moya, find the SASSA SRD section, and look for 'Update Profile Details'. However, this does not always work — the in-person SASSA office visit remains the most reliable method for a phone number change.
tips: The Moya App method works only if you are already logged into your SASSA profile on another device.
If you lost your phone entirely, the SASSA office visit is your only option.

faqs.q: Can I change my SASSA phone number online?
faqs.a: Yes — if you can still receive SMS on your current registered number. Use the 2026 SASSA Self-Service Portal at www.sassa.gov.za and update your profile under 'Contact Details'. You will receive an OTP to confirm. If you lost access to your old number entirely, you must visit a SASSA office in person with your ID document.

faqs.q: How long does it take for SASSA to update my phone number?
faqs.a: SASSA typically processes phone number changes within 3 to 7 working days. You will receive an SMS confirmation on your new number once the update is complete.

title: How to Use the Moya App for SASSA SRD: Status Checks & Banking Updates
description: The Moya App is a free data-free messaging platform that now offers SASSA SRD services. Learn how to check your status, update banking details, and appeal using Moya.
imageAlt: Smartphone displaying app icons including a messaging app

steps.title: Download and Install the Moya App
steps.content: Go to the Google Play Store (Android) or Apple App Store (iOS) and search for 'Moya App'. The app is developed by biNu and is free to download. Moya offers free data for certain services, including SASSA SRD, meaning you can check your status without using your mobile data. This makes it especially useful for users who cannot afford data or have run out of airtime.
tips: The Moya App is about 15MB to download — use WiFi if you are worried about data costs.
Make sure your phone number is the same one you registered with SASSA.

steps.title: Find the SASSA SRD Section
steps.content: Once installed, open Moya and look for the 'SASSA SRD' or 'SRD Grant' section on the home screen or in the services menu. The app has a simple, icon-based interface. Tap on the SASSA SRD icon to open the service. If you do not see it immediately, use the search bar at the top and type 'SASSA'.
tips: The Moya App interface may change with updates — the SASSA section is usually near the top.
Treat srd.sassa.gov.za as the authoritative source for your status — the app should show the same information.

steps.title: Check Your SRD Grant Status
steps.content: Inside the SASSA section, select 'Check Status'. You will be prompted to enter your 13-digit South African ID number. After entering it, your current SRD status for the most recent month will be displayed. The app shows the same information as the official srd.sassa.gov.za portal but in a simpler, mobile-friendly format.
tips: The Moya App shows only the latest month's status — use the SRD portal for your full history.
You do not need to re-enter your ID every time — Moya saves it securely.

steps.title: Update Your Banking Details via Moya
steps.content: A key feature of the Moya App is the ability to update your SASSA banking details directly. Select 'Update Banking Details' from the menu. Enter your new bank name, account number, and branch code. The account must be registered in your name. Submit the update and wait for confirmation. This is often faster than using the SRD portal for banking changes.
tips: Double-check your account number — a single wrong digit will cause payment failures.
Bank updates via Moya usually take 3 to 5 working days to be verified.

steps.title: Submit an Appeal Through Moya
steps.content: You can also submit a SASSA SRD appeal using the Moya App. Go to the 'Appeals' section in the SASSA menu. Select the month you want to appeal, choose the reason for your decline, and write a short explanation. The app submits your appeal directly to the Independent Tribunal (ITSAA). You will receive a reference number for tracking.
tips: Keep your reference number — you need it to check your appeal status.
The Moya App appeal process is identical to using the ITSAA website.

faqs.q: Is the Moya App safe for SASSA SRD services?
faqs.a: The Moya App is a popular free-data channel that routes into SASSA's SRD system and is widely used to check status and update details. Always verify your final status on the official portal at srd.sassa.gov.za before acting on what the app shows, and only download Moya from the official Google Play or Apple App Store.

faqs.q: Do I need internet data for the Moya App SASSA services?
faqs.a: No. Moya offers free data for SASSA SRD services. You can check your status, update banking details, and submit appeals without using your mobile data allowance.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA USSD Codes: Check Your Grant Status Without Internet (2026)
description: Dial these USSD codes from any cellphone to check your SASSA grant status without data. The SRD status code is *120*69277#. This guide also covers the Postbank site locator (*120*355#), the official Postbank SMS balance service, and codes that are not officially published.
imageAlt: Old-style mobile phone keypad showing keypad dialing

steps.title: What Are USSD Codes and Why Use Them?
steps.content: USSD (Unstructured Supplementary Service Data) codes work like instant commands for your phone. You dial a short code, press send, and information appears on your screen within seconds. Unlike apps or websites, USSD does not need internet data. It works on any phone, including feature phones, on any South African mobile network. The most useful SASSA code is *120*69277#, which checks your SRD R370 status.
tips: The SASSA SRD status code is free to dial.
Keep your 13-digit ID number ready before you dial.

steps.title: Dial *120*69277# for SRD R370 Status
steps.content: Dial *120*69277# and press call. This is the dedicated code for SRD R370 grant status checks. After the menu appears, select the status option and enter your 13-digit ID number when prompted. The system tells you your status for the current month: Approved, Pending, Declined, or another status. This code reads the same database as the online SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za.
tips: This code is for the SRD R370 grant, not permanent grants.
Check after the 15th of the month for the most reliable result.

steps.title: Dial *120*355# to Find Postbank Sites
steps.content: Dial *120*355# to locate your nearest Postbank site. Postbank publishes this code on its official website and on sassa.gov.za. Use it to find where you can get a Postbank Black Card (the replacement for the SASSA Gold Card, which stopped working on 31 August 2026) or to find ATM and branch services. It is a locator, not a balance check.
tips: Write down the site addresses before your phone session times out.
Bring your South African ID or temporary ID when you visit.

steps.title: Check a Postbank Balance by SMS, Not USSD
steps.content: Postbank does not publish a USSD code for balance enquiries. The official balance check is by SMS: from the cellphone number registered on your account, send 'BAL', a space, then the last four digits of your Postbank account number (not the card number) to 32302. It costs about R1 and the balance returns by SMS. You can also use a Postbank ATM or call 0800 53 54 55. Be wary of USSD balance codes circulating online - Postbank does not publish one.
tips: Account number and card number are different - use the account number.
A wrong phone number gets you an 'invalid cell number' reply.

steps.title: The Old *134*7737# SRD Code (Unverified)
steps.content: The code *134*7737# appears on some websites as an SRD application or status code. It is not listed on the official sassa.gov.za pages covered in our research, and its availability is unverified. Do not rely on it for applying or reapplying. The confirmed way to apply for the SRD grant is the official portal at srd.sassa.gov.za, and the confirmed status code is *120*69277#.
tips: When in doubt, use the portal - it is the source of truth.
Never pay anyone who claims to 'activate' a code for you.

steps.title: Troubleshooting USSD Issues
steps.content: If a USSD code does not work, ensure you are dialing exactly the right number including the asterisks and hash, check that you have network signal, switch the phone off and on, or insert your SIM into a different phone. If the code still fails, call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11. Some networks block certain USSD codes - ask your network provider to unblock them.
tips: Do not add any extra numbers before or after the code.
A 'Service Not Available' message usually clears within an hour.

steps.title: Other Ways to Check Your Status Without a Smartphone
steps.content:
If USSD is not working, three other channels check your status without data:
  • Toll-free helpline: call 0800 60 10 11 from any phone. Follow the prompts and have your 13-digit ID number ready.
  • SASSA WhatsApp line: message 082 601 0111 to check your SRD status and review status.
  • A trusted helper: a family member or community worker can check for you online at srd.sassa.gov.za. Only share your ID number with someone you trust completely.
If none of these work, visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and a staff member can look up your status.
tips: Never share your banking PIN or card PIN with anyone offering to check your status.
Keep your 13-digit ID handy before you dial or call.

faqs.q: Are SASSA USSD codes free?
faqs.a: The SRD status code *120*69277# and the Postbank site locator *120*355# are free to dial. The Postbank SMS balance enquiry to 32302 costs about R1 per message. USSD balance codes from unofficial lists are not confirmed.

faqs.q: Which code shows my SRD payment date?
faqs.a: *120*69277# shows your current SRD status, including whether you are Approved and any payment information shown for the month. For your exact 'Pay Day' date, the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za is the authoritative source.

faqs.q: Can I check my Postbank card balance by USSD?
faqs.a: Postbank does not publish a USSD balance code. Use the official SMS service (send BAL plus the last four digits of your account number to 32302, about R1), a Postbank ATM, or call 0800 53 54 55. Balance USSD codes shared on websites, such as *120*69#, are unverified.

faqs.q: What is the *120*3210# code I keep seeing?
faqs.a: *120*3210# appears on some third-party lists as a SASSA status code. It is not published on the official sources we verify against, so treat it as unverified and prefer *120*69277# for SRD status.

faqs.q: Can I check someone else's SASSA status for them?
faqs.a: Yes, with their ID number and permission, on the SRD portal, via the WhatsApp line 082 601 0111, or through *120*69277#. Only do this for people you trust, and never pass their ID number on.

title: SASSA WhatsApp Numbers 082 601 0111 and 082 046 8553: Status, Reviews and Proof of Life
description: SASSA runs two official WhatsApp channels. The self-service line 082 601 0111 checks SRD status, review status and proof-of-life checks. This guide shows the verified flow and what WhatsApp cannot do.
imageAlt: WhatsApp chat interface on a smartphone screen

steps.title: Use These Two Official SASSA Numbers
steps.content: SASSA has two official WhatsApp channels. The self-service line is 082 601 0111. It handles Social Grants self-service, including SRD application status, review status and proof-of-life checks. The older SRD line is 082 046 8553 and is still active. Both appear on the official sassa.gov.za website. Every other number you find online is a scam lookalike. No SASSA WhatsApp service costs money, and no SASSA official ever asks for your banking PIN or card PIN in a chat.
tips: Save both numbers in your phone contacts so you do not mistype them later.
If someone texts you from any other number claiming to be SASSA, block and report them.

steps.title: Start the Chat and Verify Your Identity
steps.content: Open WhatsApp, message 082 601 0111 and send the word 'Hi'. The reply walks you through the self-service menu. Pick 'Social Grants', then choose the grant you need help with. When asked, enter the mobile number you registered with SASSA, the one-time PIN sent to it, and your 13-digit ID number. This identity step is how SASSA matches the chat to your grant. The same chat works for the SRD grant and the permanent grants.
tips: Use the phone number you gave SASSA when you applied.
Wait for the next message instead of tapping through fast - the steps run in order.

steps.title: Check Your Application Status
steps.content: After your identity is confirmed, select the application-status option. The reply shows your status for the latest month - Approved, Pending or Declined - drawn from the same database as srd.sassa.gov.za. If you are approved, the reply may also show your Pay Day date. Status can change month to month because SASSA re-checks income and records every cycle, so a status from last month says nothing about this month.
tips: Check the SRD portal as well if the WhatsApp reply and your expectations differ.
A Pending status is normal early in the month - verification runs mid-month.

steps.title: Use the Review and Proof-of-Life Options
steps.content: If SASSA flagged your grant for a review or a proof-of-life check, the self-service includes a review-status option. This is the 'Am I in Review?' pathway announced with the 2026 WhatsApp launch. Use it to confirm your review status instead of waiting for an SMS. Proof-of-life checks still have to be completed through the official eLife process or at a SASSA office in some cases - the WhatsApp option confirms your status first, so you know what is still needed.
tips: Complete any proof-of-life or review step before your payment month closes to avoid a gap.
Need a review date? Check the fourth-payment-day guide for review-batch timing.

steps.title: What WhatsApp Cannot Do - Use the Portals for These
steps.content: WhatsApp is for status and review checks, not for every task. Banking details changes, a new SRD application, and appeals against a decline are all done on the official websites. Update banking details and reapply on srd.sassa.gov.za, and appeal a decline on srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za. Anything or anyone telling you that WhatsApp can fix a declined grant or change your bank details is not an official SASSA service.
tips: Keep your SRD portal login safe - it is the only place you update banking details.
Appeals are free and run for 90 days from the decline date.

steps.title: Recognise WhatsApp Scams
steps.content: A real SASSA WhatsApp chat never asks for money, your banking PIN, your card PIN or your account password. It never promises to 'unlock', 'release' or 'speed up' a payment in exchange for a fee. If a chat asks for your OTP, it is a scam - SASSA sends OTPs to your phone for you to enter into an official flow, and never asks you to read them out. Report anything that looks wrong to the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.
tips: SASSA deposits approved grants automatically - nobody can charge a 'release' fee.
Forward suspicious chats to yourself first so there is a record before you report them.

faqs.q: Is 082 601 0111 the only official SASSA WhatsApp number?
faqs.a: No. SASSA has two official WhatsApp channels: the self-service line 082 601 0111 and the older SRD line 082 046 8553. Both are listed on sassa.gov.za. Any other number claiming to be SASSA is a scam.

faqs.q: Can I check my SRD status on WhatsApp without data?
faqs.a: WhatsApp needs at least a small data connection. If you have no data, dial the USSD code *120*69277# or call the toll-free helpline 0800 60 10 11 instead.

faqs.q: Does the WhatsApp line give me my payment date?
faqs.a: When your status is Approved, the status reply often includes your Pay Day date. The SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za is the authoritative place to confirm it.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a declined grant through WhatsApp?
faqs.a: No. Appeals are lodged on the official appeals portal at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za. The WhatsApp self-service does not submit appeals.

faqs.q: Can WhatsApp fix a banking-details verification failure?
faqs.a: No. Update your banking details on the official SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za. WhatsApp is for status and review checks.

faqs.q: Will SASSA message me first on WhatsApp?
faqs.a: SASSA does not usually WhatsApp you first to ask for money or details. You start the official chat by messaging one of the two official numbers. If someone contacts you from another number with an urgent SASSA story, treat it as a scam.

title: SASSA Grant Amounts 2020–2026: Complete History & Annual Increases
description: See how every SASSA grant has changed from 2020 to 2026. Complete table of Old Age, Disability, Child Support, Foster Care, and SRD grant amounts year by year.
imageAlt: Bar chart showing financial growth over time

steps.title: SRD R370 Grant Amount History (2020–2026)
steps.content: The SRD grant started in May 2020 at R350 per month during the COVID-19 lockdown. It remained at R350 for four years. In April 2024, the grant increased to R370. It has stayed at R370 through 2025 and 2026. The 2026 Budget confirmed the grant continues until 31 March 2027 at R370. A planned transition to a Basic Income Support (BIS) grant may happen after March 2027, but no amount has been confirmed.
tips: The SRD is the only SASSA grant that has not increased since 2024.
SRD funding figures are set out in the national budget — see the National Treasury and SASSA for official amounts.

steps.title: Old Age Grant Amount History
steps.content: The Old Age Grant (also called the SASSA pension) has increased every year. In 2020, the maximum amount was R1,860 per month (60-74 years) and R1,880 (75+). By 2024, it had risen to R2,180 (60-74) and R2,200 (75+). In April 2026, the grant increased to R2,400 (60-74) and R2,420 (75+). The 75+ top-up has been R20 above the standard rate since 2020.
tips: The Old Age Grant increased by R85 in 2026 — one of the largest annual increases.
If you turned 75 during the year, your grant automatically increases.

steps.title: Disability Grant Amount History
steps.content: The Disability Grant has matched the Old Age Grant amount since 2020. It was R1,860 in 2020 and increased to R2,400 in April 2026. The grant is paid at the same rate regardless of age. Unlike Old Age, there is no higher rate for older recipients. The grant is reviewed every 6 to 12 months to confirm the disability condition persists.
tips: The Disability Grant amount is identical to the Old Age Grant (60-74 rate).
You can receive both the Disability Grant and a caregiver allowance in some cases.

steps.title: Child Support Grant Amount History
steps.content: The Child Support Grant (CSG) was R460 per month in 2020. It increased to R530 in 2024, then R560 in 2025, and reached R580 in April 2026. A R280 top-up is available for orphaned children living with relatives. The CSG is paid to the primary caregiver, not necessarily the biological parent. It covers children under 18 who meet the means test.
tips: The CSG increased by R20 in 2026 — smaller than the Old Age increase.
The R280 top-up does not count toward the means test income threshold.

steps.title: Foster Child Grant Amount History
steps.content: The Foster Child Grant was R1,070 per month in 2020. It increased to R1,250 in 2024, then R1,290 in April 2026, and R1,300 in October 2026. This grant is paid for children placed in foster care by a children's court. Unlike the Child Support Grant which continues until age 18, the Foster Child Grant can continue until age 21 if the child is still in education or training.
tips: Foster Child Grant rose by R40 in April 2026 and a further R10 in October 2026 (R1,250 to R1,290 to R1,300).
This grant is separate from and cannot be combined with the Child Support Grant.

steps.title: Future SASSA Grant Increases — Schedule and How They Work
steps.content: SASSA grant increases follow a predictable schedule. Increases are announced in the national Budget speech (usually February) and take effect on 1 April each year. The Ministry of Finance publishes a Policy Statement that sets the new amounts. A second smaller adjustment may happen in October, though this is less common. The increase cycle for 2026/2027: permanent grants increased by 3.6% to 3.7% in April 2026 (effective 1 April). The SRD R370 remained unchanged — the 2026 Budget did not allocate funds for an SRD increase. The next scheduled increase for permanent grants is April 2027, with amounts announced in the February 2027 Budget. The next possible SRD increase depends on whether the government transitions to a Basic Income Support (BIS) grant after March 2027 — no amounts have been confirmed. Important: Any claim of a grant increase that is not announced by the Ministry of Finance or SASSA official channels is false. SASSA spokesperson Paseka Letsatsi warned in May 2025: 'Any other increase not announced by credible and relevant authorities should be treated as lies.' Only trust increase announcements from National Treasury, the Ministry of Finance, and official SASSA channels.
tips: Budget speeches happen in February — check our updates page for the latest increase announcements.
The SRD has not increased since April 2024 (R350 to R370) — do not believe claims of a pending SRD increase unless confirmed by Treasury.

faqs.q: When do SASSA grant increases take effect?
faqs.a: SASSA grant increases are announced in the national Budget (usually February) and take effect on 1 April each year. The SRD grant has not increased since April 2024.

faqs.q: Will the SRD R370 grant increase in 2026?
faqs.a: No. The SRD grant has remained at R370. Permanent grants are usually adjusted once a year — check SASSA's latest published grant rates for the current amounts before relying on any figure.

faqs.q: When is the next SASSA grant increase expected?
faqs.a: The next scheduled increase for permanent grants is April 2027, announced in the February 2027 Budget. The SRD grant's future depends on whether it is extended beyond March 2027 and whether a Basic Income Support grant is introduced.

faqs.q: How can I know if a rumoured grant increase is real?
faqs.a: Only trust increase announcements from three sources: the National Treasury Budget speech (February), the Ministry of Finance Policy Statement, and official SASSA channels (www.sassa.gov.za and SASSANewsZA on Facebook). Any other source is not credible.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: Stokvel Payouts & e-Wallet Transfers: Why They Cause SASSA SRD Declines
description: Thousands of SRD applications are declined because stokvel payouts and e-wallet transfers are counted as income. Learn how to prevent and fix this.
imageAlt: Group of hands contributing money to a central pile representing a stokvel

steps.title: Understand How SASSA Detects Income
steps.content: Every month, SASSA's automated system scans your bank accounts for deposits. The system looks at all money coming into your account, regardless of where it comes from or why it was sent. If your total deposits in a calendar month exceed R624, your SRD application will be declined for that month. The system does not distinguish between salary, gifts, stokvel payouts, e-wallet transfers, or refunds — any deposit counts as income.
tips: SASSA scans all bank accounts linked to your ID number, not just one account.
Even a once-off deposit of R50 over the limit can trigger a decline.

steps.title: Why Stokvel Payouts Trigger Declines
steps.content: A stokvel is a community savings group where members contribute monthly and receive a lump sum payout in rotation. SASSA's system sees this payout as 'income' because it appears as a deposit in your bank account. A single stokvel payout of R3,000 or R5,000 will push your monthly total well over the R624 threshold. The system has no way of knowing it is a savings payout, not a salary. This is one of the most under-reported causes of SRD declines.
tips: Ask your stokvel to pay you in cash rather than bank transfer during months you need SRD.
If you received a stokvel payout, appeal and explain it was a savings withdrawal.

steps.title: Why e-Wallet Transfers Trigger Declines
steps.content: e-Wallet transfers (FNB eWallet, Capitec CashSend, Standard Bank InstantMoney) are treated as deposits by SASSA's system. If a family member sends you R700 via eWallet and you already have R200 in other deposits, your total for the month is R900 — exceeding R624 and causing a decline. The system cannot distinguish between 'family support' and 'income'.
tips: Ask family to send money via cash instead of e-Wallet during grant months.
Set up a dedicated savings account with no deposits from other people.

steps.title: How to Appeal a Stokvel or e-Wallet Decline
steps.content: Go to srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za and select the month that was declined. Choose 'Income Source Detected' as the reason. In your explanation, state clearly: 'This deposit was not income. It was a stokvel savings payout from [group name].' or 'This was a once-off family e-wallet transfer, not regular income.' Attach a bank statement showing the deposit and a letter from your stokvel group explaining the payout structure (if applicable).
tips: Be specific about the date and amount of the deposit.
If possible, get a written statement from your stokvel members confirming it was savings.

steps.title: Prevent Future Declines from Stokvel/e-Wallet
steps.content: The safest way to avoid this problem is to isolate your SRD income. Open a separate bank account that receives ONLY your SRD grant. Do not give this account number to anyone. Use a different account (or cash) for stokvel contributions, family transfers, and other financial activities. If this is not possible, ask people to send you money via cash rather than electronic transfer during the months you are receiving SRD.
tips: Many banks offer free zero-balance savings accounts — use one exclusively for SRD.
Avoid having more than one bank account active during SRD assessment months.

faqs.q: Does SASSA count stokvel payouts as income?
faqs.a: Yes. SASSA's automated system counts any deposit into your bank account as income, including stokvel payouts, e-wallet transfers, and family gifts. You must appeal if your SRD was declined due to a non-income deposit.

faqs.q: Can I receive both stokvel income and SRD grant?
faqs.a: Only if your total monthly deposits in your bank account remain below R624. If your stokvel payout pushes you over R624, you will be declined for that month. Consider receiving stokvel payouts in cash to avoid this.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: How Long Does a SASSA Appeal Take? Full 2026 Timeline & Tracking Guide
description: SASSA SRD appeals take 60 to 90 days. This guide explains the full process, what happens at each stage, how to check your appeal status, and what to do if it is taking too long.
imageAlt: Calendar with papers and a pen showing a timeline

steps.title: Submit Your Appeal (Day 0)
steps.content: The appeal process starts when you submit your appeal on the ITSAA portal at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za. You can also appeal via the SASSA WhatsApp line or Moya App. Your appeal must be submitted within 90 days of the decline. After submission, you will receive a reference number. Write this down — you need it to track your appeal. One appeal per month, one month at a time.
tips: Submit your appeal as early as possible — do not wait until the 90-day deadline.
Take a screenshot of the confirmation page showing your reference number.

steps.title: Acknowledgment Receipt (Day 1–3)
steps.content: Within 1 to 3 working days, you should receive an SMS or email confirming that the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA) has received your appeal. This acknowledgment includes your appeal reference number. If you do not receive this within 5 days, contact the SASSA helpline to confirm your appeal was logged correctly.
tips: The acknowledgment SMS comes from ITSAA, not from SASSA.
If you changed your phone number, the SMS will go to your old number — check the portal instead.

steps.title: Case Assignment & Review (Day 7–30)
steps.content: Your appeal is assigned to an independent tribunal member. The tribunal member reviews: your original application, SASSA's reason for decline, and any evidence you submitted with your appeal. The tribunal may request additional information from SASSA. During this period, your appeal status on the ITSAA portal will show as 'Appeal Pending'. No action is needed from you — you are waiting for the tribunal's decision.
tips: Do not submit a second appeal during this period — it slows down the process.
The tribunal is independent of SASSA, so they can overrule SASSA's decision.

steps.title: Decision Issued (Day 30–60)
steps.content: The tribunal makes a decision: Appeal Approved or Appeal Declined. If approved, ITSAA notifies SASSA to process payment. If declined, the letter explains why. You will receive an SMS with the outcome. You can also check the ITSAA portal using your reference number. If your appeal is approved, SASSA will pay you for the declined month within 7 to 14 working days.
tips: An approved appeal means you receive back pay for that specific declined month.
If your appeal is declined, you can request reasons in writing from ITSAA.

steps.title: What If Your Appeal Exceeds 90 Days?
steps.content: If your appeal has been pending for more than 90 days, you can escalate. Call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11 and ask for a status update on your appeal. You can also contact the Department of Social Development directly at 012 312 7726. If the delay continues, visit your nearest SASSA office with your reference number and ask them to follow up with ITSAA.
tips: Keep a log of every call — note the date, time, and who you spoke to.
Legal Aid South Africa (0800 110 110) can assist if your appeal is unreasonably delayed.

faqs.q: Why is my SASSA appeal taking more than 90 days?
faqs.a: High volumes of appeals (cause delays (SASSA does not publish exact figures). The tribunal processes appeals in order of receipt. If yours is taking longer, call 0800 60 10 11 and ask for a status update.

faqs.q: Can I check my SASSA appeal status online?
faqs.a: Yes. Go to srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za, enter your ID number and reference number, and you will see whether your appeal is Pending, Approved, or Declined.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: Why Your SASSA Grant Is Checked Every Month (Reassessment Guide 2026)
description: Unlike permanent grants, the SRD R370 is reassessed every month. Learn what changes each month, what triggers a decline, and how to keep your grant active.
imageAlt: Calendar showing monthly cycles marked with approval stamps

steps.title: How Monthly Reassessment Works
steps.content: Every month, SASSA runs an automated check on every SRD grant recipient. The system scans government databases to see if your situation has changed. It checks: Department of Home Affairs (identity still valid), your bank accounts (deposits still under R624), SARS (no new income), UIF (no unemployment benefits), and NSFAS (no student funding). If everything is fine, you stay approved. If anything changed, you may be declined for that month — even if you were approved the month before.
tips: You do not need to reapply each month — SASSA automatically reassesses you.
A decline in one month does not affect the next month — you can be approved again.

steps.title: What Triggers a Decline During Reassessment
steps.content: The most common trigger is a bank deposit that pushes your total over R624. Other triggers include: UIF records showing you received a payment, NSFAS records showing active funding, SARS records showing new employment, Home Affairs records showing identity issues, or you started receiving another SASSA grant. The system runs these checks automatically — no human reviews your application unless it is 'Referred'.
tips: Many applications are declined because of bank deposits in a given month.
A single deposit of R625 or more in a month will trigger a decline.

steps.title: How to Keep Your Grant Approved Every Month
steps.content: To maintain continuous approval: use only one bank account and ensure no one else deposits money into it, keep your total monthly deposits under R624, do not register for UIF or NSFAS while receiving SRD, complete any biometric verification within 72 hours if prompted, and keep your phone number active and up to date. If your circumstances change (you get a job, receive UIF, or start studying), update your details with SASSA honestly.
tips: Ask family and friends not to send money to your bank account during months you need SRD.
If someone must send you money, ask them to give you cash instead.

steps.title: What to Do If You Are Declined After Being Approved
steps.content: Getting declined after months of approval does not mean you did anything wrong. It may mean the system detected something new. Check your status on the SRD portal to see the specific reason. If you believe the decline is incorrect, submit an appeal within 90 days. Your grant can be reinstated for future months even without an appeal — the assessment resets each month — but an appeal is needed to get back pay for the declined month.
tips: You can be approved in January, declined in February, and approved again in March.
Always appeal declined months — you are entitled to the money if you qualify.

steps.title: October 2026: Approved One Month, Declined the Next
steps.content: The SRD grant is assessed afresh for every month. It is completely normal for your status to show 'Approved' in September and 'Declined' in October -- or the reverse -- because your circumstances are re-checked each cycle. This is not a penalty and it does not mean your grant has been cancelled. For October 2026, SASSA had not yet confirmed the SRD payment date as at 12 October 2026 -- the SRD date is announced in the last week of the month; until your status shows a 'Pay Day' date, it is normal to see 'Approved' with no date - your batch date appears once the October payment batch is released. Check your [status](/status-check) on the official portal, read what [Approved means](/status/approved), and if you were declined, appeal within 90 days to claim back pay for that month.
tips: A decline for one month never cancels your application for the next.
Check your status after the 15th of each month for the most reliable result.

steps.title: When Does Monthly Reassessment Happen?
steps.content: SASSA runs assessments continuously throughout the month, but most assessments happen in the first two weeks. If you apply in the middle of the month, you will be assessed for the following month. The payment window for approved applicants is usually the last 7 to 10 days of the month. Check your status after the 15th of each month for the most reliable result.
tips: If you applied late in the month, your first payment may take 4 to 6 weeks.
Check your status on the SRD portal or via WhatsApp between the 15th and 25th of each month.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for SRD every month?
faqs.a: No. You apply once and SASSA reassesses you automatically every month. If your circumstances change, you can update your details on the SRD portal, but you do not need to submit a new application.

faqs.q: Why was my SRD approved last month but declined this month?
faqs.a: SASSA assesses SRD eligibility fresh every single month. Approval in one month does not guarantee approval in the next, because your circumstances are re-checked against your bank accounts, UIF, SARS, NSFAS and Home Affairs records each cycle. A bank deposit that pushed your total over R624, a UIF payment received, an NSFAS record still showing as active, or a Home Affairs data update can each trigger a decline for the new month — even if nothing about your situation feels different to you. A decline for one month does not affect your application for the following month, and it does not mean you lost the grant permanently. Check the specific decline reason on the SRD portal, then see our guides for the most common reasons: [income source detected](/decline-reason/income-source-detected), [UIF registered](/decline-reason/uif-registered), [NSFAS registered](/decline-reason/nsfas-registered), and [identity verification failed](/decline-reason/identity-verification-failed). If the decline is wrong, lodge an appeal within 90 days to get back pay for that month.

title: SASSA Grants Compared: SRD vs Old Age vs Disability vs Child Support (2026)
description: Not sure which SASSA grant you qualify for? Compare all grants side by side — amounts, eligibility, age limits, means test thresholds, and how to apply.
imageAlt: Side-by-side comparison chart showing different grant options

steps.title: Grant Comparison at a Glance (2026)
steps.content: SASSA administers eight main grant types in 2026. The SRD R370 is for unemployed 18-59 year olds with income under R624/month. The Old Age Grant pays R2,400 (60-74) or R2,420 (75+) for seniors who pass the means test. The Disability Grant pays R2,400 for adults with a medical disability. The Child Support Grant pays R580 per child for caregivers earning under R5,800 (single) or R11,600 (couple). The Foster Child Grant pays R1,300 per foster child (it rose from R1,290 in October 2026). Each grant has different rules and application processes.
tips: You can only receive one SASSA grant at a time — choose the highest one you qualify for.
The SRD is the only grant that is reassessed every single month.

steps.title: Who Should Apply for the SRD R370 Grant?
steps.content: The SRD grant is best for unemployed South Africans aged 18 to 59 who have no income, no other social grant, and are not receiving UIF or NSFAS. It is the easiest grant to apply for — entirely online, no office visit needed. However, it pays the least (R370) and is not guaranteed month to month. If you are eligible for a permanent grant instead, apply for that. The SRD should be your option only if you do not qualify for any other grant.
tips: The SRD is the only grant that does not require a SASSA office visit.
If you are over 60, apply for the Old Age Grant instead — it pays R2,400.

steps.title: Who Should Apply for the Old Age Grant?
steps.content: The Old Age Grant is for South African citizens or permanent residents aged 60 and older who pass the means test. The income threshold is R9,350 per month (single) or R18,700 (married couple). The asset threshold is R1,584,000 (single) or R3,168,000 (married). You must apply in person at a SASSA office. If you are already receiving SRD and turn 60, you must switch to Old Age Grant — you cannot receive both.
tips: Apply three months before your 60th birthday to avoid a gap in payments.
The grant increases to R2,420/month when you turn 75.

steps.title: Who Should Apply for the Disability Grant?
steps.content: The Disability Grant is for adults aged 18 to 59 who have a permanent or long-term medical disability that makes them unable to work. You need a medical report from a government doctor confirming the disability. The grant pays R2,400 per month — same as Old Age. The means test thresholds are the same as Old Age. Your disability is reviewed every 6 to 12 months to confirm it still prevents you from working.
tips: Temporary disabilities (less than 6 months) do not qualify — apply for SRD instead.
If you are assessed as permanently disabled, the grant is not reviewed annually.

steps.title: Who Should Apply for Child Support Grant?
steps.content: The Child Support Grant (CSG) is for primary caregivers of children under 18 who pass the means test. The income threshold is R5,800 per month (single caregiver) or R11,600 (married couple). The grant pays R580 per child per month. You can claim for multiple children. If you are a caregiver for an orphaned child, you may qualify for the R280 top-up on top of the standard R580.
tips: The grant is paid to the primary caregiver, which can be a grandparent, aunt, or older sibling.
You do not need to be the biological parent to receive the Child Support Grant.

steps.title: Which Grant Should You Choose? Decision Guide
steps.content: Follow this decision tree: If you are over 60, apply for Old Age Grant. If you are 18-59 with a medical disability, apply for Disability Grant (R2,400 > R370). If you are caring for a child under 18, apply for Child Support Grant. If you are a foster parent, apply for Foster Child Grant. If none of the above apply and you are unemployed with no income, apply for SRD R370. You cannot receive two grants simultaneously, so choose the highest-value one you qualify for.
tips: If you qualify for both Disability and Old Age (over 60 with a disability), take Old Age.
The Foster Child Grant can overlap with other grants — it is the only exception to the one-grant rule.

faqs.q: Can I receive two SASSA grants at the same time?
faqs.a: No. You can only receive one SASSA grant at a time, with one exception: a foster parent can receive the Foster Child Grant for a foster child and also receive another grant for themselves.

faqs.q: Which SASSA grant pays the most in 2026?
faqs.a: The War Veterans Grant pays the most at R2,420 per month, followed by the Old Age Grant (75+) and Disability Grant at R2,400. The SRD pays the least at R370.

title: How to Stay Safe on SASSA Websites: Avoiding Scams & Phishing in 2026
description: Hundreds of fake SASSA websites steal ID numbers and banking details. Learn how to identify the real SASSA website and protect yourself from grant scammers.
imageAlt: Shield icon representing online security and fraud protection

steps.title: Know the Official SASSA Websites
steps.content: SASSA has only a few official websites. Committing these URLs to memory will protect you from most scams: srd.sassa.gov.za (SRD applications and status), www.sassa.gov.za (main SASSA site), srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za (appeals), and srd.dsd.gov.za (additional SRD services). Any website that looks similar but uses a different domain — like sassa-status-check.co.za, srd-sassa-gov.za, or sassahelp.co.za — is fake. Scammers buy domains that look like the real one to trick you.
tips: The real SASSA websites all end in .gov.za — no exceptions.
Bookmark the official URLs in your browser so you never type them from memory.

steps.title: Never Pay to Apply for a Grant
steps.content: SASSA grant applications are 100% free. No one should ever ask you to pay to apply, check your status, or appeal a decline. Scammers often ask for 'application fees', 'processing fees', or 'expedite fees' of R50 to R200. SASSA does not charge for any of its services. If someone asks you for money, they are a scammer. Report them to the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.
tips: If it sounds too good to be true (like a 'R700 grant'), it is a scam.
No SASSA employee will ever ask for your bank PIN or password.

steps.title: Protect Your ID Number and Banking Details
steps.content: Your 13-digit South African ID number is the most valuable piece of information scammers want. Never enter it on any website unless you are 100% sure it is an official .gov.za domain. Scammers use your ID number combined with your banking details to steal money. If a website asks for your ID number AND your banking details, verify its URL carefully before proceeding. Real SASSA sites only ask for this information on srd.sassa.gov.za and sassa.gov.za.
tips: Do not share your ID number on social media, WhatsApp groups, or with strangers.
If you entered your details on a fake site, contact your bank immediately to secure your accounts.

steps.title: Spot Fake WhatsApp Numbers and SMS Messages
steps.content: SASSA runs two official WhatsApp channels: the SASSA Self-Service line at 082 601 0111 and the SRD line at 082 046 8553. Any other number — like 082 046 8554 or 082 046 8552 — is a scam lookalike. Always check the number carefully. SASSA sends status SMS messages from short codes, not from regular cellphone numbers. If you receive an SMS asking you to click a link and 'verify your grant', check the URL before clicking. Fake SMS messages often have spelling errors and create urgency ('your grant will be cancelled').
tips: SASSA will never ask you to send money via eWallet or airtime.
If an SMS says 'click here to receive your grant', it is a scam — SASSA deposits automatically.

steps.title: How to Verify Whether a SASSA News Story Is Real
steps.content: Fake SASSA news spreads rapidly on WhatsApp and Facebook. Common fake stories include promises of double grant payments, claims of 'new rules affecting your pension', and deadlines that do not exist. Before believing or sharing any SASSA news, verify it: check the official SASSA website at www.sassa.gov.za, visit the official SASSA Facebook page (SASSANewsZA), call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11, or check our updates page at sassahelphub.co.za/updates where we track every official announcement. Red flags that a SASSA news story is fake: the story promises extra or double payments, claims new rules that affect all beneficiaries from a specific date, uses a non-.gov.za website link, comes from a WhatsApp group or unofficial Facebook page, or asks you to click a link to 'verify your status'. SASSA National Spokesperson Paseka Letsatsi said: 'Any increase not announced by credible and relevant authorities should be treated as lies. Beneficiaries should only rely on credible sources of information on our official social media pages.'
tips: Only three sources are always credible: www.sassa.gov.za, official SASSA Facebook (SASSANewsZA), and the Ministry of Finance Budget announcements.
If a story says 'share this with all grant beneficiaries,' it is often misinformation — verify before forwarding.

steps.title: What to Do If You Are Scammed
steps.content: If you shared your ID or banking details with a fake SASSA website, take action immediately: call your bank to freeze your accounts and reverse any unauthorized transactions, report the scam website to the SASSA fraud hotline at 0800 60 10 11, open a case at your nearest police station, and change your banking details on the real srd.sassa.gov.za portal. If scammers used your ID number to apply for grants fraudulently, report this to SASSA so they can flag your ID.
tips: The SASSA fraud hotline is free and you can report anonymously.
Keep records of any fraudulent messages or websites as evidence for the police.

faqs.q: How do I know if a SASSA website is real?
faqs.a: The URL must end in .gov.za. The official SRD portal is srd.sassa.gov.za. The official SASSA site is www.sassa.gov.za. If the domain ends in .co.za, .org, .com, or any other extension, it is not an official SASSA website.

faqs.q: Someone asked me to pay R50 to check my SRD status — is this normal?
faqs.a: No. SASSA does not charge for any service. Status checks are free on the SRD portal, via USSD, and via WhatsApp. Anyone asking you to pay is a scammer.

faqs.q: How can I tell if a SASSA news story on WhatsApp is real?
faqs.a: Check three things: Is the story on the official SASSA website (www.sassa.gov.za)? Is it on the official SASSA Facebook page (SASSANewsZA)? Does it promise extra money or create panic? If the answer to the first two is no, or the third is yes, the story is fake.
