title: What to Do If SASSA Asks You to Update Your Information (Step-by-Step)
description: Received an SMS, letter, or call asking you to update your information with SASSA? Follow this step-by-step guide to respond safely, keep your grant active, and avoid scams.

steps.title: Step 1: Verify the Request Is Genuine
steps.content:
Before doing anything, confirm the request is really from SASSA. Scammers frequently send fake SMS messages and make fake calls pretending to be SASSA.

**How to Identify a Genuine SASSA Review SMS:** A legitimate SASSA review SMS comes from a recognised registered short code (not a regular cellphone number or WhatsApp). It tells you to visit a SASSA office and lists the documents you need to bring. It does NOT contain a clickable link to "verify now" or ask for your banking PIN or card PIN.

**What a Genuine Review SMS Looks Like:** "SASSA: Your grant has been flagged for review. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and proof of residence to complete the review. For enquiries call 0800 60 10 11." The message will be in plain text with no URLs, no payment demands, and no threats.

**Red Flags That Mean It Is a Scam:** The message asks you to click a link to "verify now", asks for your banking PIN or card PIN, demands payment to "process" the update, creates urgency ("update within 24 hours or your grant stops"), or comes from WhatsApp or a regular cellphone number.

**What If You Did Not Receive an SMS?** If you think you are due for a review but never received an SMS, it may be because your contact details are out of date. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID to check your review status. Update your phone number if it has changed — see our guide on [changing your registered phone number](/guides/lost-phone-number).

**August 2026:** Beneficiaries flagged for grant review will receive an SMS from SASSA about their review appointment. These SMS messages asking you to visit a SASSA office are genuine — SASSA does not send review notifications via WhatsApp or social media. [Read the full announcement](/updates/update-2026-028).

Signs of a genuine SASSA request: the SMS comes from a recognised short code (not a regular cellphone number), the message tells you to visit a SASSA office (not a website link), the letter is on official SASSA letterhead with contact details, and the caller identifies themselves with their name and office location. If you are unsure, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 to confirm before taking any action.
tips: SASSA will never ask for your PIN, OTP, or banking password — never give these to anyone.
If the message has spelling errors or comes from a WhatsApp number, it is almost certainly a scam.
When in doubt, call 0800 60 10 11 — do not use any phone number provided in the suspicious message.

steps.title: Step 2: Prepare Your Documents
steps.content: Once you have confirmed the request is genuine, gather the documents you need. The exact documents depend on why SASSA is asking you to update your information. General documents to bring: your original 13-digit South African ID book or Smart ID card (or alternative ID document if you use a permit), proof of residence (utility bill, bank statement, or lease agreement dated within 3 months), your SASSA card if you have one, and any documents that explain changes in your situation (e.g., marriage certificate if you changed your surname, proof of new income if you started working, death certificate of a spouse). Make photocopies of everything before you go.
tips: Call the SASSA office ahead of time to confirm which documents are needed for your specific update.
Keep your original documents in a separate bag from the copies — never hand over originals unless asked.

steps.title: Step 3: Visit the SASSA Office
steps.content: Go to your nearest SASSA office. Find the address and operating hours on our [SASSA offices page](/sassa-offices). Go early — offices open at 08:00 and queues form before then. When you arrive: take a queue ticket, wait for your number, explain to the officer that you are there to update your information (show them any SMS or letter you received), hand over your documents, answer any questions honestly, and ask for a confirmation slip or reference number when the update is complete. If the officer identifies additional documents needed, ask if you can bring them later the same day or if you need to make a new appointment.
tips: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday are generally less busy than Monday and Friday.
Bring water and a snack — wait times can be 2 to 3 hours at busy offices.

steps.title: Step 4: Confirm the Update Was Processed
steps.content: After your visit, the officer should confirm that your information has been updated in the system. Ask for the confirmation in writing or get a reference number. If SASSA said they would process the update and notify you, ask how long it will take — usually 3 to 7 working days for phone number changes, 1 to 2 working days for address or contact detail changes, and immediate for document verification updates. If you do not hear back within the stated timeframe, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and provide your reference number. Do not assume the update was processed if you did not receive confirmation.
tips: Write down the date, time, and name of the officer you spoke to.
Keep the confirmation slip with your other important documents.

steps.title: Step 5: Check Your Grant Status After the Update
steps.content: After your information has been updated, check your grant status to confirm everything is in order. For SRD grants, check online at srd.sassa.gov.za. For permanent grants, ask the SASSA officer to confirm your next payment date. If your grant was suspended pending the update, it should be reinstated within 7 to 14 working days. Check your status weekly after the update. If your grant has not been reinstated after 14 working days, call the SASSA helpline with your reference number.
tips: Check your status on the SRD portal between the 15th and 25th of the month for the most accurate result.
If your grant status shows 'Pending' for more than 30 days after the update, escalate to the SASSA helpline.

steps.title: Step 6: What If You Cannot Visit a SASSA Office?
steps.content: If you are too ill, disabled, elderly, or live too far from a SASSA office, you may qualify for a home visit or alternative arrangement. Call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and explain your situation. SASSA may send an official to your home to verify your documents. This service is available for beneficiaries who cannot travel. Alternatively, you can authorise a trusted family member to attend on your behalf. You must give them a signed letter of authorisation, a copy of your ID, and the original documents they need to present. The family member must bring their own ID as well.
tips: Only trust a family member or close friend to handle your SASSA documents — not a stranger or 'agent.'
If you authorise someone else, give them a specific list of what to do and ask them to bring back a confirmation slip.

faqs.q: Is the SASSA SMS asking me to update my information real or a scam?
faqs.a: It depends. Genuine SASSA SMS messages come from registered short codes and ask you to visit a SASSA office. Fake SMS messages usually contain a link to click, ask for personal information, or demand payment. When in doubt, call 0800 60 10 11 to verify.

faqs.q: What does a genuine SASSA review SMS look like?
faqs.a: A genuine review SMS comes from a registered SASSA short code, tells you to visit a SASSA office with specific documents, and does NOT contain clickable links. It will never ask for your PIN or banking details. Example: 'SASSA: Your grant has been flagged for review. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and proof of residence. Call 0800 60 10 11 for enquiries.' Any message demanding immediate payment or asking you to click a link is a scam.

faqs.q: Can I update my SASSA information online instead of visiting an office?
faqs.a: Some updates can be done online. Phone number changes, banking details, and address updates may be done through the SASSA Self-Service Portal at www.sassa.gov.za. However, if SASSA specifically asked you to visit an office, you must go in person — the online portal may not allow the type of update needed.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore the request to update my information?
faqs.a: Your grant may be suspended until you respond. SASSA cannot continue paying a grant without accurate information on file. If your grant is suspended, it can be reinstated once you update your information, and you will receive back pay.

faqs.q: How long does it take for SASSA to process an information update?
faqs.a: Simple updates (address, contact details) take 1 to 2 working days. Phone number changes take 3 to 7 working days. Document verification updates are usually processed immediately during your office visit.

title: Best Bank Accounts for SASSA Beneficiaries in 2026: Low Fees & ATM Access Compared
description: Not all bank accounts are equal when you live on a SASSA grant. Compare Capitec, Postbank, TymeBank, FNB, Absa, Nedbank, Bank Zero, and Shoprite Money Market — monthly fees, ATM withdrawal costs, and hidden charges that eat into your grant.
imageAlt: Comparison of different bank cards on a table

steps.title: What to Look for in a SASSA-Friendly Bank Account
steps.content: When you live on a SASSA grant, every rand counts. An account charging R10/month in fees eats R120 from your grant every year. An ATM charging R8 per withdrawal adds up fast. Before choosing a bank account for your SASSA grant, check: the monthly account fee (must be R0), ATM withdrawal fees (free or cheap at the bank's own ATMs), branch access for cash deposits, eWallet and CashSend fees, and whether the bank allows a zero-balance account. The best account has zero monthly fees, free or cheap ATM withdrawals, and no minimum balance. 'Free' accounts often still charge for SMS notifications, other-bank ATM withdrawals, or paper statements — read the fine print.
tips: Open your SASSA-linked bank account in your own ID name — SASSA does not pay into third-party accounts.
Avoid accounts requiring a minimum monthly deposit — skipping a month triggers penalties.

steps.title: Postbank: The Official SASSA Bank (R0/month, Free ATM Withdrawals)
steps.content: Postbank issues the SASSA Black Card. Every SASSA beneficiary qualifies. Zero monthly fee. Three free withdrawals per month at any Postbank ATM. Additional withdrawals cost R2 to R8. Free balance checks via *120*3210#. The Black Card replaced the Gold Card in 2026. If you do not have a personal bank account, Postbank is the safest option — no fees, no minimum balance, and you can withdraw at any Post Office or retail store. The downside: Postbank's mobile app is basic and customer service can be slow. But for a no-frills account costing nothing, it is the best choice if you only need to receive and withdraw your grant.
tips: Postbank ATMs are free. Using a Capitec or FNB ATM costs R2 to R8.
Keep your PIN safe — Postbank has weaker fraud protection than commercial banks.

steps.title: Capitec Global One (R0/month, R7–R10 per Withdrawal)
steps.content: Capitec is the most popular bank among SASSA beneficiaries. The Global One account has no monthly fee if you do not swipe or use online banking in a month. You pay R7.50 per withdrawal at Capitec ATMs and R10 at other banks. The Capitec app is excellent — check balances, send money, buy airtime, lock your card. Capitec has branches in almost every town. The downside: Capitec charges R1 per SMS notification and R5 for a printed statement. If you withdraw R370 twice a month at a Capitec ATM, you pay R15 in fees — 4% of your grant. Still, Capitec is the best commercial option because of its app quality and wide branch network.
tips: Use the Capitec app to check your balance — this avoids the R1 SMS fee.
Capitec ATMs at Shoprite and Checkers are free — look for the Capitec logo before inserting your card.

steps.title: TymeBank (R0/month, R7/withdrawal, 4% Cashback)
steps.content: TymeBank is a digital bank with zero monthly fees. Open an account in 5 minutes using your ID number and cellphone — no branch visit. TymeBank charges R7 per withdrawal at Pick n Pay and Boxer kiosks. The big advantage: effective 4% cashback on your first R700 spend each month when you swipe at Pick n Pay, Boxer, or The Spaza Shop. For SASSA beneficiaries shopping at these stores, you get roughly R28 back on R370 spend. TymeBank also offers a savings pocket paying up to 11% interest. The downside: no physical branches — everything is done through the app or at Pick n Pay kiosks.
tips: Open your TymeBank account at any Pick n Pay or Boxer kiosk — takes 5 minutes.
Use your TymeBank card for all Pick n Pay purchases to earn the 4% cashback.

steps.title: Shoprite Money Market (Cash Collection, Not a Bank Account)
steps.content: The Shoprite Money Market is not a bank account. It lets you collect your SASSA grant in cash at any Shoprite, Checkers, or Usave till point. No account needed — bring your ID and SASSA card. No monthly fee, no ATM fee. Best for beneficiaries who do not have a bank account and prefer cash. The downside: collection during store hours only (08:00 to 20:00), queue at customer service, no online banking or deposits. For SRD beneficiaries receiving R370, it is practical if you live near a Shoprite.
tips: Avoid collecting in the first week of the month — queues are longest then.
Count your cash at the counter before walking away.

steps.title: FNB Easy, Absa Flexi, Nedbank Pay-as-Use Compared
steps.content: FNB Easy: R0/month, R10/withdrawal at FNB ATMs, R12 at other banks. Good app but higher fees than Capitec. Absa Flexi: R0/month, R10/withdrawal at Absa ATMs. Fewer rural branches. Nedbank Pay-as-Use: R0/month, R8/withdrawal at Nedbank ATMs. None match Capitec or TymeBank for low fees and rural accessibility. Bank Zero is new with R0 fees and R2 withdrawals at its own ATMs, but very few ATMs nationwide so far. For pure SASSA grant management, Capitec and TymeBank are the best value.
tips: Never use private ATMs at taxi ranks — some charge up to R15 per withdrawal.
Check your bank's ATM locator on their app before leaving home.

steps.title: Comparison Table: Best Bank Accounts for SASSA (2026)
steps.content:
Side-by-side summary:
Postbank Black Card — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: Free (3/month), R2–R8 after. Access: Post Offices nationwide. Best for: Free, no-frills banking.
Capitec Global One — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R7.50 (own ATM), R10 (other). Access: Excellent, most towns. Best for: Good app + wide branches.
TymeBank — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R7 (Pick n Pay/Boxer). Access: Pick n Pay stores only. Best for: Cashback on groceries.
Shoprite Money Market — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: Free at counter. Access: Shoprite/Checkers. Best for: Cash-only users near Shoprite.
FNB Easy — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R10. Access: Good in cities. Best for: Existing FNB customers.
Absa Flexi — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R10. Access: Moderate. Best for: Existing Absa customers.
Bank Zero — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R2 (own ATM). Access: Limited. Best for: Tech-savvy urban users.
tips: Choose one bank and stick with it — multiple accounts mean more accounts for SASSA to scan.
If you switch banks, close your old account to reduce accounts linked to your ID.

faqs.q: Which bank is best for SASSA beneficiaries in rural areas?
faqs.a: Capitec has the widest rural branch network. Postbank is also widely available through Post Offices, but hours are shorter.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Postbank to Capitec for my SASSA payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Update your banking details on the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za. The change takes effect the following month.

faqs.q: Does opening a second bank account affect my SRD grant?
faqs.a: Yes — SASSA scans all accounts linked to your ID. Stick to one account and keep it clean of non-grant deposits.

faqs.q: Are there truly free bank accounts in South Africa?
faqs.a: Postbank Black Card is the only fully free account. TymeBank and Capitec have no monthly fees but charge per ATM withdrawal.

faqs.q: Does SASSA force me to use a specific bank?
faqs.a: No. SASSA does not require you to use any particular commercial bank. You can choose your own bank, use Postbank, or collect cash at a participating retailer.

title: Fix Missing SASSA Grant Payments
description: Your SASSA grant did not arrive? Learn why payments get delayed, how to check your status, and the exact steps to get your money back into your account.

steps.title: Wait 2–3 Business Days After the Official Payment Date
steps.content: Before you panic, check the calendar. Banks do not always process SASSA deposits on the same day. If your Pay Day was yesterday and the money is not in your account yet, wait at least 2 to 3 business days. This is especially true for standard bank accounts — Capitec and FNB often credit same-day, but Absa, Nedbank, Standard Bank, and smaller banks can take 1 to 3 days. Postbank Black Card credits are usually instant. If your status on the SRD portal says 'Approved' with a Pay Day, but you cannot see the money yet, wait the full 3 business days before taking further action. Check your [SASSA status online](/status-check) first to confirm the Pay Day.
tips: Capitec and FNB usually reflect payments within hours — if it has been 3 days with them, something is wrong.
SASSA payment dates are staggered — your neighbours may be paid on different days depending on grant type.

steps.title: Check Your SASSA Status Online — Is It Approved with a Pay Day?
steps.content: The single most important thing to check is your official SASSA status. Go to the [SASSA status check page](/status-check) and enter your 13-digit ID number. If your status shows 'Approved' with a specific Pay Day, the money has been allocated to you and the problem is likely a bank delay or incorrect banking details. If your status shows 'Pending' or 'Declined', the issue is with your application, not the payment. If it shows 'Referred' or 'Under Review', your grant is being reviewed — you may be scheduled for the Fourth Payment Day (see Step 4). Always check the official portal before calling anyone.
tips: Your online status is the source of truth — SMS notifications can be delayed or not sent at all.
If you cannot access the portal, use the SASSA USSD code *120*69277# to check from any phone.

steps.title: Verify Your Banking Details Are Correct and Your Account Is Active
steps.content: A very common cause of 'Approved but not paid' is incorrect or outdated banking details. Log into the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za or the main SASSA website and review the bank account linked to your grant. Check: the bank name is correct, the account number has no missing or swapped digits, the branch code is correct, the account is open and active, and the account is registered in YOUR name — SASSA does not pay into third-party accounts. If the account was closed, frozen, or you changed banks and forgot to update SASSA, the payment will bounce back. Read our guide on [how to change your SASSA banking details](/guides/bank-details-pending-fix).
tips: Even one wrong digit in your account number will cause payment failure — re-type it carefully.
If you recently switched from a Gold Card to a Postbank Black Card, your banking details may have changed.

steps.title: Check If Your Payment Was Moved to the Fourth Payment Day
steps.content: If your grant is flagged for review - for example, due to a means test or identity verification issue - SASSA pays you on a special fourth payment day instead of the normal three-day payment cycle. If your status shows 'Referred', 'Under Review', or you received an SMS from SASSA asking you to visit an office, your payment may have been moved to the fourth day. Check the [SASSA Payment Calendar](/payment-calendar) for the confirmed fourth payment date each month. If you still have not been paid after the fourth payment day, you must visit a SASSA office with your ID to resolve the review status. In August 2026 the fourth payment day fell on Friday, 7 August - that is historical information; the current month's date may differ. Read our [fourth payment day guide](/guides/fourth-payment-day-guide) for the full explanation.
tips: Fourth payment day is typically the first Friday or Monday after the normal three-day cycle ends.
Being on fourth payment day means SASSA flagged your account — complete the review to return to normal payments.

steps.title: Check for SMS Notifications About Reviews or Life Certification
steps.content: SASSA frequently sends SMS messages to beneficiaries about outstanding actions. Check your phone's SMS inbox for messages from SASSA short codes. Look for: a request to complete life certification (also called eLife certification or annual verification), a request to visit a SASSA office for a review of your information, or a notice that your grant requires biometric verification. If SASSA sent you an SMS and you did not respond, your payment may have been held. Check our guides on [life certification](/guides/life-certification) and [biometric verification](/guides/biometric-fix-guide) for step-by-step help. If you lost the phone number registered with SASSA, you may have missed these SMS messages — follow our [lost phone number guide](/guides/lost-phone-number) to update it.
tips: SASSA sends multiple reminder SMS before holding a payment — check your spam or archived messages too.
If you changed your phone number, you will not receive SMS notifications until you update it with SASSA.

steps.title: Contact SASSA Toll-Free on 0800 60 10 11
steps.content: If you have checked all the above and your payment has still not arrived, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11. The call is toll-free from any South African network. Before you call, get these ready: your 13-digit ID number, the phone number registered with SASSA, your banking details so they can verify what is on file, and the Pay Day date shown on your status. Explain clearly: 'My SASSA status says Approved with a Pay Day of [date], but the money has not reflected in my account.' The agent can check whether the payment was released, bounced back, or held for review. Ask for a reference number for your call. If the agent cannot resolve your issue, ask to speak to a supervisor or request an escalation.
tips: Call early in the morning (08:00) — afternoon wait times can exceed 30 minutes.
The helpline is open Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 16:00 — do not call on weekends.

steps.title: Visit Your Nearest SASSA Office as a Last Resort
steps.content: If you have tried all the steps above and still have not received your payment, visit your nearest SASSA office in person. Bring: your original South African ID book or Smart ID card, proof of residence (utility bill or bank statement), a printed copy of your SASSA status showing 'Approved' (if you can print one), and any SMS notifications from SASSA. Explain to the SASSA officer that you have not been paid despite an 'Approved' status. The officer will investigate and may process a manual payment or resolve the review flag on your account. This is a last resort — SASSA offices have long queues, so go early (before 08:00) and be prepared to wait. Find your nearest office on the [SASSA offices page](/sassa-offices).
tips: Bring water and a snack — queues at busy SASSA offices can take 2 to 3 hours.
If you are elderly or disabled, ask a trusted family member to accompany you or call 0800 60 10 11 to request a home visit.

faqs.q: How long should I wait before reporting a missing SASSA grant payment?
faqs.a: Wait at least 3 full business days after your official Pay Day. Banks process SASSA deposits at different speeds — Capitec and FNB are usually same-day, while other banks may take 1 to 3 days. If your status says 'Approved' but the money has not arrived after 3 business days, start investigating.

faqs.q: My SASSA status says 'Approved' but no money came — what's wrong?
faqs.a: This usually means one of three things: (1) A bank delay — wait 3 business days. (2) Incorrect or outdated banking details — check and update them on the SRD portal. (3) Your grant is under review and you have been moved to the Fourth Payment Day — check the SASSA Payment Calendar for the date.

faqs.q: My old age grant didn't arrive for 3 months — what should I do?
faqs.a: Three months of non-payment is serious and likely means your grant has been suspended. Common causes: you missed the annual life certification deadline, SASSA flagged you for a review you did not attend, or your banking details are incorrect. Call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 immediately and visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID. If your grant was suspended due to non-verification, complete the verification and you will receive back pay. See our guide on [how to reinstate a suspended grant](/guides/guide-reinstate-grant).

faqs.q: Can SASSA deduct money from my grant without telling me?
faqs.a: SASSA can deduct money from your grant only in specific circumstances and only with your written consent. Authorised deductions include: funeral policy premiums (if you signed up), loan repayments to SASSA-accredited lenders (if you took a loan against your grant), and medical aid contributions (if you opted in). SASSA cannot deduct money for unauthorised reasons. If you see unexpected deductions, call Postbank at 0800 53 54 55 to check if it is a card deduction, or call SASSA at 0800 60 10 11 to report unauthorised deductions.

A reversed or bounced payment means the bank rejected the deposit — usually because the account number is wrong, the account is closed, inactive, or not in your name. The money goes back to SASSA and is held, not lost. Fix your banking details on the official SRD portal as soon as possible (see our bank details fix guide, /guides/bank-details-pending-fix), then wait for the next payment cycle or collection. While your details are wrong, you can still collect your grant in person at a SASSA pay point with your ID. For permanent grants, update your details at a SASSA office.

title: SASSA Gold Card to Black Card Guide
description: The SASSA Gold Card switch-off date (31 August 2026) has passed. Find out what happens if you still have a Gold Card, whether you can still access your grant, and how to get your free Postbank Black Card now.

steps.title: The Gold Card Switch-Off (31 August 2026) - What Changed
tips: The replacement is still free after the deadline - no one should charge you for it.
Your grant payments continue to be paid into your Postbank account regardless of which card you hold.
steps.content: SASSA and Postbank announced that SASSA Gold Cards stopped working after 31 August 2026 at ATMs, retail stores and payment points. That deadline has now passed. The free replacement is the Postbank Black Card, and it is still available. If your Gold Card has stopped working, the fix is simple: get your free Black Card from any Postbank service point.

steps.title: What If You Still Have a Gold Card?
tips: Help elderly or disabled family members make the switch too.
Your PIN stays the same on the Black Card as it was on your Gold Card.
steps.content: If you still have a Gold Card, it may no longer work at ATMs or retail points. Do not wait - collect your free Postbank Black Card as soon as possible so you can access your money. The Black Card is linked to the same Postbank account as your Gold Card, so your banking details with SASSA do not change and no balance is lost. Your money remains safe in your Postbank account.

steps.title: What If Your Gold Card Stopped Working?
tips: Do not throw your old Gold Card away until your Black Card is working.
If a card reader rejects your card, ask the cashier whether the store participates in SASSA cash collection before assuming the money is lost.
steps.content: If your Gold Card has stopped working, you can still access your grant. Your grant is still paid into your Postbank account every month. Until you have a Black Card, you can collect your money in person by presenting your South African ID at a SASSA pay point or designated retail collection point. The reliable long-term fix is to collect your free Postbank Black Card so your card works normally again.

steps.title: Where to Get Your Free Postbank Black Card
tips: Look for the Postbank desk inside the store - usually near customer services.
You can collect the card at any location in any province, not just where you registered.
steps.content: You can collect your free Postbank Black Card at any Postbank service point located inside these retail stores nationwide: Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer, and Spar. You do not need to go to a SASSA office for this - Postbank handles the card migration directly. There are hundreds of service points across all nine provinces, so there is likely one near you.

steps.title: What to Bring - and It's FREE
tips: You do not need proof of residence, bank statements, or any other documents.
If anyone asks you to pay for the card, report them immediately.
steps.content: Bring your valid South African ID document (Smart ID card or green ID book). A temporary ID is also accepted. The entire process is FREE - there are no fees, no hidden charges, and no forms to fill in. The new Black Card is activated immediately when issued. Any money remaining on your old Gold Card transfers automatically to the new Black Card, so you will not lose any funds.

steps.title: How to Find Your Nearest Postbank Service Point
tips: The USSD code *120*355# works on any phone - no internet needed.
Save the Postbank helpline 0800 53 54 55 in your phone contacts.
steps.content: To locate the closest Postbank service point, dial *120*355# from any cellphone. This USSD code is free and works on all South African networks (Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, Telkom). You will receive an SMS with the address of your nearest collection point. You can also call Postbank toll-free on 0800 53 54 55 for assistance.

steps.title: What If You Are in Another Province?
tips: Postbank service points operate during standard retail hours, typically 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays.
Go mid-week and mid-morning for the shortest queues.
steps.content: You can collect your Black Card at any Postbank service point in any province - it does not have to be the one where you registered. Service points are located inside Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer, and Spar stores nationwide, including rural towns. If you cannot reach a service point, call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 to arrange an alternative, or ask a SASSA mobile unit in your area for assistance.

steps.title: Who Handles Card Problems?
tips: SASSA handles grants; Postbank handles cards. Use the right channel.
For lost or stolen cards, call 0800 53 54 55 immediately to block the card.
steps.content: SASSA offices do not handle card replacements or card-related problems. The Postbank Black Card is managed entirely by Postbank. If you lose your card, it gets stolen, or you have any card-related issue, go directly to a Postbank service point or call the Postbank helpline on 0800 53 54 55. Going to a SASSA office for card issues will waste your time - they cannot help you with Postbank cards. For grant payment problems that are not card-related, contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11.

steps.title: What Should You Do If Money Is Not Accessible?
tips: Do not panic - an uncollected grant stays in your Postbank account until you access it.
Never pay anyone who offers to 'unlock' or 'withdraw' your grant for a fee - it is a scam.
steps.content: If your money is not accessible, work through these steps: (1) confirm your status is 'Approved' with a 'Pay Day' date on the official portal; (2) check whether your grant is under review - you may be paid on the fourth payment day; (3) if you collect at a retail point, wait for the payment SMS before going to the store; (4) if your card is declined at an ATM, try a retail pay point or a Postbank branch; (5) if the money has genuinely not been paid, follow our missing grant payment guide (/guides/missing-grant-payment-guide) before calling 0800 60 10 11. Your grant does not disappear - it accumulates in your account if uncollected.

faqs.a: Your Gold Card may no longer work at ATMs or retail stores after the 31 August 2026 switch-off. Your grant is still paid into your Postbank account and the money is safe. Collect your free Postbank Black Card from any Postbank service point to access your money normally again.
faqs.q: What happens if I still have a Gold Card?

faqs.a: You can still access your grant. Until you get a Black Card, present your South African ID at a SASSA pay point or designated retail collection point to collect your money. For a long-term fix, collect your free Postbank Black Card from a service point.
faqs.q: What if my Gold Card stopped working?

faqs.a: Yes. Your grant continues to be paid into your Postbank account every month and is never lost. You can collect it in person with your ID, or normally once you have your Black Card.
faqs.q: Can I still access my grant?

faqs.a: Yes, the replacement is completely free. There are no fees, no forms to pay for, and no hidden costs. If anyone asks you to pay for the card, it is a scam. Report them to Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 or the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.
faqs.q: Is the Black Card replacement free?

faqs.a: Bring your valid South African ID - a Smart ID card, green ID book, or temporary ID. You do not need proof of residence, bank statements, or any other documents. The process takes minutes and the card is issued immediately.
faqs.q: What documents are required for the replacement?

faqs.a: At any Postbank service point located inside Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer, or Spar stores nationwide, in any province. Use the free USSD code *120*355# or call 0800 53 54 55 to find your nearest service point.
faqs.q: Where can I get the replacement?

faqs.a: You can collect your Black Card at any Postbank service point in any province. It does not have to be where you originally registered. If you cannot reach one, call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 to arrange an alternative.
faqs.q: What if I am in another province?

faqs.a: Postbank handles all card matters, not SASSA. For lost, stolen or faulty cards, or any card question, contact Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 or visit a Postbank service point. Contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 only for grant payment issues that are not card-related.
faqs.q: Who handles card problems?

faqs.a: Check your status on the official portal for your 'Pay Day' date, confirm your grant is not under review, and wait for the payment SMS if collecting at retail. If the money has genuinely not been paid, follow the missing grant payment guide and call 0800 60 10 11. Your grant accumulates safely in your Postbank account if uncollected.

title: Grant Under Review? Fourth Payment Day
description: If SASSA paid you on a different day than other beneficiaries, your grant may be under review. Here is what the fourth payment day is, why it happens, and what you must do to get back on the normal payment cycle.

steps.title: What Is the Fourth Payment Day?
tips: The fourth payment day is always the day after Children's Grants are paid.
If you are unsure whether you were paid on the fourth day, check the date of your last deposit.
steps.content: SASSA normally pays social grants over three working days: Older Persons Grants first, then Disability Grants, then Children's Grants. A fourth payment day is used for beneficiaries whose grants have been selected for review. If you receive your grant on the fourth day, it means SASSA needs you to complete a grant review. This is not a penalty - it is a standard verification process required by the Social Assistance Act. You are still receiving your money; you just need to take an extra step afterward.

steps.title: Why Can Some Beneficiaries Be Paid Later?
tips: Your neighbours may be paid on a different day to you - that is normal.
Your 'Pay Day' date on your status is the date to trust, not the general schedule.
steps.content: Not every beneficiary is paid on the same day. The first three days cover grants that have passed all checks. Beneficiaries whose grants are under review - for example, because their details are being re-verified or their income needs to be re-assessed - are paid on a separate fourth day once their review status is cleared for that month. Your own pay day depends on your grant type, your review status, and whether your banking details have been verified.

steps.title: What Does a Review Have to Do with Payment?
tips: Being under review is not a decline - it is a temporary check.
You are still paid while your grant is under review, just on the fourth day.
steps.content: A review is a check that you still qualify for the grant. When your grant is selected for review, SASSA holds your payment until the review is processed so it can confirm your details are correct. In months when your grant is under review, you are paid on the fourth payment day instead of your normal day. Completing the review returns your grant to the standard three-day cycle from the following month.

steps.title: What Does 'Under Review' Mean?
tips: Read your status message carefully - it tells you whether anything is needed from you.
Do not reapply while your grant is under review - it can cause confusion.
steps.content: 'Under review' means SASSA is re-checking your eligibility. It can be triggered by a routine data verification, a means-test re-assessment, a change in your personal details, or an identity check. Your status on the portal may show 'Referred' or 'Under Review'. It does not mean your grant has been cancelled. See our guide on the grant review and verification process (/guides/grant-verification-process) for what happens during the check.

steps.title: How Will You Know SASSA Needs Something From You?
tips: Keep your cellphone number and address updated with SASSA at all times.
If you changed your number recently, visit SASSA to update it immediately.
steps.content: SASSA notifies beneficiaries selected for review via SMS before the payment cycle begins. The SMS explains that your grant has been flagged for review and that you will be paid on the fourth payment day. Check your phone messages carefully - the SMS may come from an official SASSA number. If you missed the SMS because your contact details are outdated, you will only discover you are under review when your payment does not arrive on the normal day. If you did not receive an SMS, check your status on the official portal - it is the source of truth.

steps.title: Check Your Review Status on the Official WhatsApp Line
tips: The WhatsApp status check works on Android; iPhone users should use the SRD portal.
The same official line handles review and proof-of-life checks for selected beneficiaries.
steps.content: You do not have to wait for an SMS. The official SASSA self-service WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) can show your status without airtime. Send 'Hi' to the number, pick your grant type, and verify your identity with your mobile number and one-time PIN. If your grant has been flagged for a review, use the review/proof-of-life option to confirm your identity instead of waiting for a notification. This is a genuine service run by SASSA, not a third party. Our WhatsApp guide (/guides/sassa-whatsapp) walks through the menus step by step.

steps.title: What Documents May Be Requested?
tips: Make copies of all documents before going to the office.
Bring a pen - you may need to fill out forms at the office.
steps.content: When visiting a SASSA office for your review, bring: your original 13-digit South African ID document (smart card or green ID book), proof of your current residence (utility bill or affidavit), proof of income if applicable (payslip or bank statements for the last 3 months), and any grant-specific documents (medical reports for disability grant, birth certificates for child support grant). Having all documents ready will ensure the review is completed in one visit.

steps.title: What Happens After a Review?
tips: Complete the review within the same month - do not delay until the next payment cycle.
If you are bedridden or frail, contact SASSA about a home visit option.
steps.content: After the review is complete, SASSA updates your record. If you still qualify, your grant returns to the normal three-day payment cycle from the following month. If the review finds a problem - such as a data mismatch or income above the threshold - your grant may be declined for that month, and you can appeal. Some beneficiaries can complete the review online through the SASSA eLife Certification portal using facial recognition, and selected beneficiaries can also confirm their review on the official SASSA WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) using the proof-of-life option - see our life certification guide. The eLife portal has known technical issues - if it fails after several attempts, visit an office. See our eLife certification troubleshooting guide (/guides/elife-certification-troubleshooting) for help.

steps.title: Historical Example: August 2026 (Already Passed)
tips: Do not assume October has a confirmed fourth payment date - as at 12 October 2026 SASSA had not announced it yet.
Your status is the only reliable source for your personal pay day.
steps.content: This is historical information for context only. In August 2026, SASSA announced that beneficiaries whose grants were under review would be paid on Friday, 7 August 2026 - the fourth payment day for that month, after Older Persons (4 August), Disability (5 August) and Children's Grants (6 August). That date has passed. For the current month, check the SASSA payment calendar (/payment-calendar) for the confirmed dates and the latest announcement in our latest confirmed payment dates update.

steps.title: What If You Were Approved but Did Not Receive Payment?
tips: Capitec and FNB usually reflect payments within hours - other banks can take 1 to 3 days.
Your online status is the source of truth - SMS can be delayed.
steps.content: If your status shows 'Approved' but you have not received payment, do not panic. Wait 2 to 3 business days after your Pay Day date for the banking system to reflect the deposit, then check: your banking details are correct and the account is active, you have received the payment SMS if collecting at retail, and your status has not changed to 'Referred' or 'Under Review'. If the money still has not arrived, follow our missing grant payment guide (/guides/missing-grant-payment-guide) step by step before calling the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11.

steps.title: What If You Did Not Receive an SMS?
tips: Check your spam or archived messages too - notifications can land there.
Never share an SMS verification code with anyone.
steps.content: SASSA SMS messages can be delayed or not sent at all. If you believe your grant may be under review but received no SMS, check your status on the official SRD portal with your 13-digit ID number. If your status shows 'Referred', 'Under Review', or a 'Pay Day' date that has passed without payment, contact the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11. If you changed your phone number and never updated SASSA, follow our lost phone number guide (/guides/lost-phone-number) to fix it.

steps.title: What Should You Do in the Next Payment Cycle?
tips: Check your status at the same time each month so you notice changes early.
Keep your banking details current with SASSA to avoid payment delays.
steps.content: Once your review is complete and your grant is back on the normal cycle, keep your details up to date: keep your registered phone number active, do not let anyone else deposit into your bank account, complete any biometric or life certification checks promptly, and check your status after the 15th of each month. If your status is 'Approved', look for a 'Pay Day' date; if it is 'Declined', appeal within 90 days. This keeps your grant on track month after month.

faqs.a: You were likely selected for a grant review. SASSA pays beneficiaries under review on a separate fourth payment day, which is always the day after Children's Grants are paid. Check your status on the official portal for your review status and 'Pay Day' date.
faqs.q: Why did I receive my grant on a different day than other beneficiaries?

faqs.a: It means SASSA is re-checking that you still qualify for the grant. It is not a decline and does not cancel your grant. You are paid on the fourth payment day while the review is processed, and you must complete the review to return to the normal three-day cycle.
faqs.q: What does it mean if my grant is under review?

faqs.a: If you do not complete the review, your grant will be suspended in the next payment cycle. You will not receive payments until the review is done. Continued failure to respond may cause your grant to lapse, requiring a new application. Complete the review as soon as possible after receiving your fourth-day payment.
faqs.q: What happens if I don't complete my grant review?

faqs.a: Some beneficiaries can use the eLife Certification portal to complete the review online via facial recognition. However, the portal has known technical issues. If the online method fails after several attempts, you must visit a SASSA office in person. Green ID book holders should plan to visit an office directly.
faqs.q: Can I complete the review online instead of visiting an office?

faqs.a: No. As at 12 October 2026 SASSA had not yet officially confirmed a fourth payment date for October 2026. Do not rely on third-party dates. Check the official SRD portal for your 'Pay Day' date and the SASSA payment calendar (/payment-calendar) for the latest confirmed dates.
faqs.q: Is there a confirmed fourth payment day for October 2026?

faqs.a: Wait 2 to 3 business days after your Pay Day date, confirm your banking details are correct, and check whether your status is 'Referred' or 'Under Review'. If the money still has not arrived, follow our missing grant payment guide (/guides/missing-grant-payment-guide) and call SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 if needed.
faqs.q: What if I was approved but did not receive my payment?
Can I check my review status on WhatsApp?
faqs.a: Yes. Message the official SASSA self-service line at 082 601 0111, send 'Hi', pick your grant type, and verify your identity with your mobile number and OTP. If SASSA has flagged your grant for a review, use the review/proof-of-life option to confirm your status without waiting for an SMS. The status check works well on Android; iPhone users should use the SRD portal.

title: Fix SASSA eLife Certification Problems
description: eLife portal keeps loading? Facial recognition fails? OTP not received? This guide covers every known eLife Certification glitch and how to fix it.

steps.title: What Is eLife Certification and Why Is It Required?
steps.content: eLife Certification is SASSA's online identity verification system. It uses facial recognition technology to confirm that you are still alive and eligible to receive your grant. SASSA introduced it on 30 March 2026 as a digital alternative to in-person grant reviews. Most users complete it successfully, but some run into problems. If you are among those who cannot complete it, this guide will help you troubleshoot.
tips: eLife Certification is required once every 12 months for most beneficiaries.
If the online method fails, you can still complete the review at a SASSA office.

steps.title: Problem: The Portal Keeps Loading and Never Opens Your Profile
steps.content: Many beneficiaries report that after entering their details, the system 'keeps loading and never goes through to my profile.' This is usually caused by high traffic, connectivity issues with the Department of Home Affairs interface, or using an outdated browser. Solution: Try accessing the portal during off-peak hours (early morning before 08:00 or after 18:00). Clear your browser cache and cookies. Try a different browser (Chrome or Edge work best). If using mobile data, switch to WiFi or vice versa.
tips: Peak hours are 09:00 to 15:00 on weekdays — avoid these times.
The portal works best on Google Chrome on a smartphone.

steps.title: Problem: Facial Recognition Fails After Multiple Attempts
steps.content: The most common complaint is facial recognition failing after 10, 20, or even 30 attempts. This happens because SASSA's system relies on the Department of Home Affairs database, which may have a low-quality photo (especially for green ID book holders). Solution: Ensure you are in a well-lit room with a plain background. Remove glasses, hats, and face coverings. Hold the phone steady at eye level. If you have a green ID book, the photo on Home Affairs' system may be too old — you will need to visit a SASSA office for fingerprint verification instead.
tips: Natural daylight works best — avoid harsh overhead lighting.
If you have a green ID book, go directly to a SASSA office rather than struggling online.

steps.title: Problem: OTP (One-Time PIN) Not Received or Marked as Wrong
steps.content: Some beneficiaries receive the OTP but the system says it is wrong. Others never receive the OTP at all. This is usually a network delay or a mismatch between the number you entered and the number registered with SASSA. Solution: Wait 10-15 minutes and request a new OTP — do not rush. Ensure you are entering the exact cellphone number registered with your SASSA application. If you changed your number, the OTP goes to your old number and you cannot access the portal.
tips: OTPs expire after 5 minutes — request a new one if time runs out.
If you changed your phone number, visit a SASSA office to update it first.

steps.title: Problem: 'Department of Home Affairs Not Available' Error
steps.content: This error means the SASSA system cannot connect to the Home Affairs database to verify your identity. It is not a problem with your details — it is a system error. Solution: Wait and try again later — the issue is usually temporary. If the error persists for more than 3 days, visit a SASSA office. SASSA has confirmed it is working on direct connectivity to DHA to reduce these interruptions, but the fix is still being implemented.
tips: This error is more common during weekends and public holidays.
SASSA staff can complete fingerprint verification even when the online system is down.

steps.title: Problem: You Never Received the Verification Link from SASSA
steps.content: Some beneficiaries say SASSA never sent the SMS with the verification link. This may be because your phone number is outdated, your SIM is not RICA-registered, or the SMS was blocked by your network. Solution: Check that your SIM is RICA-registered in your name. Ensure your phone number is the same one registered with SASSA. Contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 to request the link be resent. If the link never arrives, visit a SASSA office for in-person verification.
tips: Some networks block bulk SMS — ask your provider to unblock SASSA messages.
Until you complete verification, your grant status may show 'Self-Correction Required'.

steps.title: Final Option: Visit a SASSA Office for Fingerprint Verification
steps.content: If you have tried all troubleshooting steps and still cannot complete eLife Certification online, visit your nearest SASSA office. SASSA staff can complete fingerprint biometric verification, which is more reliable than facial recognition. In practice, fingerprint verification tends to be more reliable than facial recognition for SASSA biometric checks. Bring your original South African ID document.
tips: Fingerprint verification is faster and more reliable — do not hesitate to use it.
Visit early in the morning (before 09:00) to avoid the longest queues.

faqs.q: Why does the eLife Certification portal keep failing?
faqs.a: The portal relies on the Department of Home Affairs database, which can experience connectivity issues. Other causes include high traffic during peak hours, outdated browser, or a poor-quality photo on the Home Affairs system (common for green ID book holders). Try during off-peak hours, clear your cache, and use a different browser.

faqs.q: I tried facial recognition 20 times and it still failed — what now?
faqs.a: Visit your nearest SASSA office for fingerprint verification. In practice, fingerprint verification is usually reported as more reliable than facial recognition for SASSA checks. It is the more reliable method. Bring your original South African ID document.

faqs.q: How long does eLife Certification take to process?
faqs.a: Once you successfully complete the facial recognition, the verification is processed immediately. Your grant status usually updates within 24 hours. If you complete fingerprint verification at a SASSA office, the update is also immediate.

title: SASSA Grant Deductions Explained
description: Money missing from your SASSA grant? Learn about loan repayments, funeral policies, and other deductions — and how to stop unauthorised ones.

steps.title: Common Types of SASSA Grant Deductions
steps.content: SASSA deducts money from grants for several legitimate reasons. The most common deductions are: loan repayments to SASSA-accredited micro-lenders (if you took a loan against your grant), funeral policy premiums (if you signed up for a policy linked to your grant), electricity prepaid vouchers (in some municipal areas), school feeding scheme contributions (in certain provinces), and administration fees for payment collection at certain retail points. Not all deductions apply to every beneficiary, and some are optional.
tips: You have the right to know what is being deducted and why.
Most deductions require your written consent before they can be applied.

steps.title: How to Check What Is Being Deducted
steps.content: If you see money missing from your grant, you can check the reason in several ways. Call the SASSA toll-free helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and ask for a breakdown of deductions. Visit your nearest SASSA office and request a payment history printout. Check your SMS notifications — SASSA sometimes sends details of deductions by SMS. Check your bank statement for the name of the organisation receiving the deduction. If a deduction is active that you did not authorise, you have the right to dispute it.
tips: Keep your SMS and bank statements as evidence of deductions.
Ask for a transaction history report at any SASSA office.

steps.title: Loan Deductions from SASSA-Accredited Lenders
steps.content: If you took a loan from a SASSA-accredited micro-lender (such as Mzansi Loans, JUMEME, or similar lenders), the lender may deduct repayments directly from your grant. These deductions are legal but regulated. The maximum amount that can be deducted is 33.3% of your grant. You have the right to cancel the debit order directly with the lender or through SASSA. If deductions continue after the loan is fully repaid, contact SASSA immediately.
tips: Never give your SASSA card or PIN to a lender as 'security' for a loan.
If a lender takes more than 33.3% of your grant, report them to SASSA.

steps.title: Funeral Policy Deductions
steps.content: Some funeral insurance companies partner with SASSA to deduct premiums directly from beneficiary grants. If you signed up for a funeral policy and agreed to premium deductions, you will see monthly deductions on your grant payment day. These deductions must be authorised by you in writing. If you no longer want the policy, contact the insurer directly to cancel. If deductions continue after cancellation, report it to SASSA.
tips: Read the terms of any funeral policy carefully before signing.
You can have multiple deductions stopped by visiting a SASSA office.

steps.title: What to Do If a Deduction Is Wrong or Unauthorised
steps.content: If you believe a deduction is incorrect, unauthorised, or continuing after it should have stopped: first, check your grant payment history at a SASSA office to identify exactly which organisation is making the deduction. Second, contact the organisation directly and request a refund. Third, if they do not resolve the issue, contact the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11. Fourth, if the deduction is causing financial hardship, request a suspension of all deductions at your nearest SASSA office. SASSA can stop all third-party deductions from your grant if you demonstrate hardship.
tips: Do not ignore deductions — the longer they continue, the more money you lose.
If an unauthorised deduction persists, lodge a formal complaint with SASSA.

steps.title: Can You Opt Out of All Deductions?
steps.content: Yes, in most cases you can opt out of voluntary deductions. Loan repayments can only be stopped once the loan is fully repaid. Funeral policy deductions can be cancelled by contacting the insurer. Electricity and school feeding deductions require you to contact your municipality or school to opt out. If you are experiencing financial hardship, visit a SASSA office and request a 'deduction suspension' — SASSA has the authority to pause most third-party deductions temporarily.
tips: SASSA cannot stop deductions for debt repayments ordered by a court.
Request everything in writing and keep copies of all correspondence.

faqs.q: Why is money being deducted from my SASSA grant?
faqs.a: Money may be deducted for loan repayments, funeral policy premiums, electricity prepaid vouchers, or school feeding contributions. Most deductions require your written consent. Check your payment history at a SASSA office to see exactly what is being deducted and by whom.

faqs.q: Can I stop deductions from my SASSA grant?
faqs.a: Yes, for most voluntary deductions. Contact the organisation making the deduction (loan provider, insurer, municipality) and request cancellation. If they do not stop, visit a SASSA office and request a deduction suspension. Loan repayments cannot be stopped until the loan is fully repaid.

faqs.q: How do I check what is being deducted from my grant?
faqs.a: Call SASSA on 0800 60 10 11, visit a SASSA office for a payment history printout, or check your bank statement for the name of the organisation receiving the deduction.

steps.title: Choose where to bank first

steps.title: Gather your documents

steps.title: Make sure the account is in your own name
steps.content: Your SASSA payment must go to an account that matches your ID exactly. An account in someone else's name, or with a spelling mismatch, will be rejected and your payment will be delayed.

faqs.q: How long before my grant pays into the new account?
faqs.a: After you update your details on the SASSA/SRD portal, verification typically takes a few working days. Your next payment batch will use the corrected account once verification is complete.

faqs.q: What if I don't want a bank account?

title: How to Replace Your Lost or Stolen SIM Card in South Africa (2026)
description: Step-by-step: block your old SIM, visit a network store with your ID, and get a new SIM that keeps your number — important if your number is linked to SASSA.

steps.title: Report the loss and block your number
steps.content: Contact your network (Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, or Telkom) as soon as possible to block the SIM so no one can use it. Most networks have a USSD or app option, or you can visit a store.
tips: Act quickly — a blocked SIM cannot be used for SIM-swap fraud.
Have your ID number ready when you call.

steps.title: Find your nearest network store
steps.content: A SIM swap usually requires visiting a branded store with your ID. Some networks also allow RICA-compliant online or in-app replacements — check the network's official website for the current process.
tips: Avoid informal 'agents' offering SIM swaps — use the official store.

steps.title: Take your proof of identity
steps.content: Bring your original South African ID book or smart ID card (or passport plus visa for foreign nationals) and any RICA documents you have.
tips: RICA rules require the registered owner to be present.

steps.title: Get the SIM swapped to your number
steps.content: The consultant deactivates the old SIM and activates a new one against your existing number. Your number stays the same; only the physical SIM changes.
tips: Test the new SIM with a call before you leave the store.

steps.title: Re-link important services
steps.content: Once the new SIM is active, verify you can receive SMS and access WhatsApp and the SRD portal. If your number actually changed, update SASSA with your new number using our lost phone number guide.

faqs.q: Will I lose my number?
faqs.a: No. A SIM swap keeps your existing number; only the physical SIM card changes.

faqs.q: How much does a SIM swap cost?
faqs.a: Fees vary by network and change over time. Check the current fee on the network's official website before you go.

faqs.q: Can someone else collect my SIM for me?
faqs.a: No. RICA rules require the registered owner to be present with their ID.

title: The Official SASSA Websites: SRD Portal, Services Portal and Appeals Portal
description: There are three official SASSA websites for three different jobs: srd.sassa.gov.za for the R370, services.sassa.gov.za for permanent grants, and srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za for appeals. This guide maps each site and shows how to spot fakes.
imageAlt: Laptop screen showing a government services website

steps.title: Know the Three Official SASSA Websites
steps.content: Every official SASSA website ends in .gov.za. Each one has a different job, so use the right site for the right task: | Website | What it is for | |---|---| | srd.sassa.gov.za | SRD R370: apply, reapply, check monthly status, update banking details | | services.sassa.gov.za | Permanent grants (older persons, disability, child support, foster, care dependency, grant-in-aid): apply and track | | srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za | Appeal a declined SRD grant (the Independent Tribunal) | | sassa.gov.za | Forms, office finder, payment schedule, official announcements |
tips: Bookmark these four addresses so you never click a lookalike site again.
If the address does not end in .gov.za, it is not an official SASSA site.

steps.title: Use the SRD Portal for Your R370 Grant
steps.content: Sign in at srd.sassa.gov.za with your 13-digit ID number and the cellphone number you registered with SASSA. A one-time PIN (OTP) arrives by SMS and codes each login. On this portal you can apply, reapply, check whether your status is Approved, Pending or Declined, and change the bank account your grant is paid into. There is no trick to it - the OTP step is what keeps outsiders out of your grant.
tips: Always use the phone number you gave SASSA when you applied.
Your status can change month to month - check the portal rather than relying on memory.

steps.title: Use the Services Portal for Permanent Grants
steps.content: services.sassa.gov.za is where permanent grant applications happen - older persons, disability, child support, foster child, care dependency and the rest. You create an applicant profile with your ID and phone number, then apply for the grant, upload supporting documents and track progress. Approved permanent grants are also reviewed periodically, and the portal shows review status.
tips: Keep scanned copies of your supporting documents - the portal asks you to upload them.
A permanent grant review does not cancel the grant - it rechecks that you still qualify.

steps.title: Use the Appeals Portal to Challenge a Decline
steps.content: If SASSA declines your SRD grant for a month, you can challenge it free of charge at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za - the Independent Tribunal. You choose the declined month and the reason SASSA gave, explain your situation, upload supporting proof and note your reference number. Appeals must be lodged within 90 days of the decline. Successful appeals are paid the back pay for the declined month.
tips: Submit one appeal per declined month - each month is a separate case.
Keep your reference number; you use it to track the appeal.

steps.title: Register and Sign In Smoothly
steps.content: The portals share one rhythm: your 13-digit ID plus your registered cellphone number, then an OTP by SMS. If the system says your details are not found, you are almost always on the wrong phone number - one from before a SIM swap or one you never registered. Update your cellphone number on the SRD portal first, then carry on. Passwords are case-sensitive, and each portal keeps its own login.
tips: Lost your number since you applied? Fix it before you try to register.
Write your portal password somewhere safe - shared, not complex.

steps.title: Spot Fake Sites and Fake Apps
steps.content: Fake SASSA portals are the most common SASSA scam online. They look like the real thing, end in domains like .co.za or .com, and ask for banking PINs or card numbers while promising to 'unlock' or 'release' a payment. The real portals never ask for your banking PIN, card PIN or password, and the grant is never behind a fee. The SRD grant has no official smartphone app. When in doubt, open a trusted link from sassa.gov.za itself.
tips: The real SRD grant costs nothing to apply for, check or appeal - anyone charging a fee is a scammer.
Type the portal address yourself instead of tapping links in SMS messages.

faqs.q: Is it free to use the official SASSA websites?
faqs.a: Yes. Applying, checking status, updating banking details and appealing are all free on the official portals. Anyone who charges you to 'process' these is scamming you.

faqs.q: Can I apply for permanent grants on the SRD portal?
faqs.a: No. Use services.sassa.gov.za for permanent grants and srd.sassa.gov.za for the SRD R370. The two systems are separate.

faqs.q: Why can't I register on a SASSA portal?
faqs.a: The usual cause is a cellphone number mismatch. Register and log in with the number you gave SASSA when you applied. If you changed numbers, update it on the SRD portal first.

faqs.q: Is there an official SASSA app?
faqs.a: No. SASSA has announced a mobile app is in development, but no official SRD app exists yet. Every 'SASSA app' on app stores today is third-party or a scam.

faqs.q: How do I know I'm on a real SASSA site?
faqs.a: Real SASSA addresses end in .gov.za: srd.sassa.gov.za, services.sassa.gov.za, srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za and sassa.gov.za. Anything claiming to be SASSA that does not end in .gov.za is fake.

title: SRD Reapplication: When You Must Reapply and When You Must Not
description: You apply for the SRD R370 once - SASSA reassesses you every month. This guide explains the only times you really do need to reapply (status 'reapplication_required'), how to do it at srd.sassa.gov.za, and why a declined month needs an appeal, not a new application.
imageAlt: Person filling in an application form on a phone

steps.title: You Apply Once - SASSA Reassesses Every Month
steps.content: The SRD R370 application stays active after you submit it. You do not reapply each month. What happens every month is an automated recheck of your circumstances: your bank account deposits, UIF records, NSFAS status, SARS records and Home Affairs identity details. If nothing changed, you stay Approved. If something is flagged, you go to Declined for that month only. Your status flipping between months is normal, not a cancellation.
tips: Check your status after the 15th of the month for the most reliable result.
Approved in one month does not guarantee Approved in the next - circumstances are rechecked.

steps.title: A Decline Is Not a Cancellation - Appeal, Don't Reapply
steps.content: If SASSA declines you for a month, submit an appeal, not a new application. SATSA declines carry a reason code (income source detected, identity verification failed, UIF registered, NSFAS registered and others). Read the code, then appeal that specific month at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za within 90 days. Successful appeals are paid back pay. Reapplying when you are simply declined creates duplicate applications, which can flag your account and delay a genuine application.
tips: One appeal per declined month - each month is a separate case.
Appeals are free and take about 60 to 90 days.

steps.title: The One Status That Means You Really Must Reapply
steps.content: If your status on the SRD portal shows reapplication_required (also seen as 'Reapplication Pending'), SASSA no longer holds an active application for you. That is different from a decline - it means your application lapsed, timed out or was administratively reset. Common causes: a compulsory reapplication window you did not refresh, an internal application expiry, a platform migration that did not carry older applications across, or a cancellation after a period of ineligibility (for example a UIF period). This reason cannot be appealed - the fix is a fresh application.
tips: Not sure why you were reset? Check your status on srd.sassa.gov.za before acting.
Reapplication_required is one of the few reasons where reapply, not appeal, is the correct move.

steps.title: How to Reapply Step by Step
steps.content: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za and sign in with the same 13-digit ID number and cellphone number you used before. Submit a new application and answer every question honestly - the system cross-checks your answers against government databases. Since September 2025 the grant also uses biometric verification, so complete the facial scan or fingerprint step within the 72 hours if you are prompted, otherwise the application can stall. Then check your status around the 15th.
tips: Use the exact same ID number and phone number as your old application.
Do not create a second profile - reuse the one already on file.

steps.title: What Reapplication Does and Does Not Give You
steps.content: A successful reapplication restores your grant from the current month's assessment onward. It does not automatically back-pay the months your application was lapsed. If some of those lapsed months are still inside the 90-day appeal window, appeal those months as well - in some cases SASSA has approved backdated payments for declined months even after a reapplication. Approved grant amounts flow to the payment method on file, so keep your banking details up to date too.
tips: Appeal declined months alongside reapplying instead of waiting to see what happens.
Back pay is decided per month and per appeal - it is not automatic.

steps.title: Keep Your Application Active and Healthy
steps.content: Future resets are avoidable. Keep the cellphone number on your file current so SASSA can notify you and code your OTPs. Use one bank account and make sure nobody else's deposits push you over the R624 income line. Complete biometric verification within 72 hours when prompted. Update your details honestly when your situation changes. And never pay an agent to reapply for you - the official portal is free.
tips: Lost your phone number? Update it on the SRD portal (see our phone-number guide).
A single stranger depositing into your account can tip you over the threshold.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for the SRD grant every month?
faqs.a: No. You apply once and SASSA reassesses your eligibility automatically every month. Reapply only when your status tells you to, such as 'reapplication_required'.

faqs.q: I was declined this month - should I reapply?
faqs.a: No. A declined month is not a cancellation. Read the decline reason on the SRD portal and appeal that month within 90 days at srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za if you disagree. Reapplying instead can cause duplicate applications.

faqs.q: What does the 'reapplication_required' status mean?
faqs.a: It means SASSA no longer has an active application for you - usually because it lapsed, timed out or was administratively reset. It is not an eligibility decline and cannot be appealed. You need to submit a fresh application at srd.sassa.gov.za.

faqs.q: How long does a new SRD application take to process?
faqs.a: A few weeks in most cases. Check your status on the SRD portal after the 15th of the month. First you see Pending, then Approved with a Pay Day, or Declined with a reason.

faqs.q: Will reapplication back-pay the months my grant was lapsed?
faqs.a: No, not automatically. Reapproval applies from the current month's assessment. If declined months are still within the 90-day appeal window, appeal them separately for possible back pay.

faqs.q: Can I reapply if I cancelled my SRD application myself?
faqs.a: Yes. Go to srd.sassa.gov.za and submit a new application with the same ID number and phone number. Your eligibility is then reassessed from the current month.

title: SASSA Grant Balance Check: Bank USSD Codes, Postbank SMS and Card Tips
description: How to check your SASSA grant balance depends on where the money lands. Verified USSD codes for Capitec, FNB, Standard Bank, Absa and Nedbank, the official Postbank SMS balance service, and the difference between a balance and an SRD status.
imageAlt: Person holding a mobile phone and a bank card

steps.title: Your Payment Channel Decides How to Check
steps.content: There is no single 'SASSA balance check'. The right method depends on where your grant is paid: into your own bank account, or onto a Postbank card (Black Card, or the old Gold Card). If SASSA pays into your bank, you check with that bank. If it pays onto a Postbank card, you check with Postbank. Meanwhile the SRD portal shows your application status - whether the grant was approved for a month - not the rand balance sitting on your card or in your account.
tips: Check the pay-day notification first; the balance follows the payment.
Which method applies to you? Look at how your money arrived last month.

steps.title: Bank Account Payments: Verified USSD Codes
steps.content:
If your SRD grant is paid into a normal bank account, dial your bank's cellphone banking code to check the balance - no data needed. These codes were verified against official bank pages:

| Bank | Balance check (dial) |
|---|---|
| Capitec | *120*3279# |
| FNB | *120*321# |
| Standard Bank | *120*2345# |
| Absa | *120*2272# |
| Nedbank | *120*001# |
| African Bank | *120*225# |

You may need your cellphone banking PIN the first time. Each bank still lists its code on its own website and on the back of its card - confirm there before relying on it.
tips: Register your cellphone number with the bank first - USSD banking is tied to it.
These codes use airtime in some cases, not data, and most balance checks are free or a few cents.

steps.title: Postbank Cards: Use the Official SMS Balance Service
steps.content: Postbank's official balance check is by SMS, published on the Postbank website. From the cellphone number registered on your account, send: 'BAL', a space, then the last four digits of your Postbank account number (not the card number) to 32302. You get your balance back by SMS; it costs about R1. Send it from a different phone and you get an 'invalid cell number' error. You can also use a Postbank ATM balance enquiry for free, or call 0800 53 54 55.
tips: Account number and card number are different - use the account number.
Save the number 32302 in your phone so the SMS is quick to send on pay day.

steps.title: *120*355# Is a Site Locator, Not a Balance Code
steps.content: The code *120*355# helps you find your nearest Postbank site - it is not a balance enquiry. Notably, Postbank does not publish a USSD balance code at all. The *120*69# balance menu you will see on some websites is not from Postbank and is unverified. Stick to the confirmed methods: the SMS service above, a Postbank ATM, or the call centre.
tips: A website telling you to 'dial this code for your SASSA balance' is usually seeking clicks, not helping.
Never enter your PIN into a USSD session sent to you by SMS - dial only the codes you trust.

steps.title: Balance vs Status - They Are Two Different Things
steps.content: The USSD code *120*69277# and the SRD portal tell you your grant status - Approved, Pending or Declined, and the Pay Day date when approved. They do not show what is left on your card or in your bank account. To see the actual money, use your bank's USSD/app/ATM (bank payments) or Postbank's SMS service (card payments). Two queries, two answers: status says you were approved, balance says the money is there.
tips: Approved with no payment arrived yet? The Pay Day date on the portal tells you what day to expect it.
Declined for the month? That is a status problem, not a balance problem - you may need to appeal.

steps.title: Check Safely, Especially on Pay Day
steps.content: On pay day the networks are congested - if a USSD or SMS request times out, wait a few minutes and retry. Never share your banking PIN, card PIN or OTP with anyone who contacts you about a 'balance check'. If your Postbank card locks after three wrong PIN attempts, you must visit a branch or service point. And if your balance looks short, check recent deposits against the R624 income line, because one stranger's deposit can trigger a declined month.
tips: SASSA will never call and ask you to 'verify' by reading out an OTP or PIN.
Blocked card? Visit any Postbank service point - you will not sort it over SMS.

faqs.q: Do I need internet data to check my SASSA balance?
faqs.a: No. USSD and SMS balance checks work without data on any phone. They may use a small amount of airtime, but no data bundle is required.

faqs.q: Is the Postbank SMS balance service free?
faqs.a: No - it costs about R1 per enquiry. The balance reply arrives by SMS from the registered cellphone number only.

faqs.q: Can I check my Postbank card balance by USSD?
faqs.a: Postbank does not publish a USSD balance code. The official methods are the SMS service (send BAL plus the last four digits of your account number to 32302), Postbank ATM, or the call centre on 0800 53 54 55. USSD codes circulating online, like *120*69#, are unverified.

faqs.q: What is the *120*69277# USSD code for?
faqs.a: It is the SASSA SRD status check - it shows whether your SRD grant is Approved, Pending or Declined for a month, not how much money is on your card.

faqs.q: My SRD is paid into a bank account. How do I check the balance?
faqs.a: Use that bank's own channel - Capitec *120*3279#, FNB *120*321#, Standard Bank *120*2345#, Absa *120*2272#, Nedbank *120*001#, or each bank's app and ATM.

faqs.q: Why does my balance look lower than expected?
faqs.a: Check recent deposits first. If a deposit pushed your total over the R624 income threshold in a month, that month may be declined. Check your SRD status on the portal, and appeal within 90 days if the decline is wrong.
